+# myHCMUS Frontend Constitution
 
 ## Core Principles
 
-### [PRINCIPLE_1_NAME]
-<!-- Example: I. Library-First -->
-[PRINCIPLE_1_DESCRIPTION]
-<!-- Example: Every feature starts as a standalone library; Libraries must be self-contained, independently testable, documented; Clear purpose required - no organizational-only libraries -->
+### I. App Router and TypeScript First (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
-### [PRINCIPLE_2_NAME]
-<!-- Example: II. CLI Interface -->
-[PRINCIPLE_2_DESCRIPTION]
-<!-- Example: Every library exposes functionality via CLI; Text in/out protocol: stdin/args ΓåÆ stdout, errors ΓåÆ stderr; Support JSON + human-readable formats -->
+All application code MUST use the Next.js App Router and TypeScript. Routes live under `src/app`,
+and route grouping such as `(public)` and `(protected)` MUST be preserved. Strict type safety is
+mandatory: no `any` in new production code, no type assertions used to bypass validation, and no
+JavaScript source files for application logic. Server Components MUST be the default; `"use client"`
+is added only when interactivity, browser APIs, or client-only hooks require it.
 
-### [PRINCIPLE_3_NAME]
-<!-- Example: III. Test-First (NON-NEGOTIABLE) -->
-[PRINCIPLE_3_DESCRIPTION]
-<!-- Example: TDD mandatory: Tests written ΓåÆ User approved ΓåÆ Tests fail ΓåÆ Then implement; Red-Green-Refactor cycle strictly enforced -->
+Rationale: the App Router and TypeScript are the project's established foundation, and their
+consistent use keeps routing, rendering, and data boundaries predictable.
 
-### [PRINCIPLE_4_NAME]
-<!-- Example: IV. Integration Testing -->
-[PRINCIPLE_4_DESCRIPTION]
-<!-- Example: Focus areas requiring integration tests: New library contract tests, Contract changes, Inter-service communication, Shared schemas -->
+### II. Feature-First Architecture (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
-### [PRINCIPLE_5_NAME]
-<!-- Example: V. Observability, VI. Versioning & Breaking Changes, VII. Simplicity -->
-[PRINCIPLE_5_DESCRIPTION]
-<!-- Example: Text I/O ensures debuggability; Structured logging required; Or: MAJOR.MINOR.BUILD format; Or: Start simple, YAGNI principles -->
+Business capabilities MUST be organized as self-contained features under
+`src/features/<name>/` with the internal structure `components/`, `hooks/`, `services/`,
+`types/`, and `mappers/`, creating each directory only when the feature needs it. Feature code
+MUST NOT import another feature's internals directly; cross-feature reuse happens through shared
+modules in `src/libs`, `src/components`, or `src/types`. Application routes remain thin and MUST
+delegate behavior to feature modules.
 
-## [SECTION_2_NAME]
-<!-- Example: Additional Constraints, Security Requirements, Performance Standards, etc. -->
+Rationale: feature isolation limits coupling, makes ownership clear, and prevents the application
+from collapsing into a shared pile of unrelated modules.
 
-[SECTION_2_CONTENT]
-<!-- Example: Technology stack requirements, compliance standards, deployment policies, etc. -->
+### III. Centralized HTTP Through the API Client (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
-## [SECTION_3_NAME]
-<!-- Example: Development Workflow, Review Process, Quality Gates, etc. -->
+All HTTP communication MUST go through `src/libs/api-client.ts` (imported as `@/libs/api-client`).
+Direct use of `fetch`, `axios`, `XMLHttpRequest`, or any other transport outside that module is
+prohibited. Features MUST NOT construct base URLs; the API client owns base URL resolution,
+headers, serialization, and error normalization. New transport behavior MUST be added to the
+shared API client rather than reimplemented per feature.
 
-[SECTION_3_CONTENT]
-<!-- Example: Code review requirements, testing gates, deployment approval process, etc. -->
+Rationale: one transport boundary guarantees consistent authentication, error handling, and
+observability, and prevents divergent network behavior across features.
 
+### IV. Service Contracts with Paired Mock Implementations (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
+
+Every feature MUST expose its data operations through a service contract: a TypeScript
+`interface` in `features/<name>/services/`. Each contract MUST have two implementations: a real
+implementation that calls the API client, and a mock implementation that returns deterministic
+fixtures with simulated latency. Both MUST implement the same interface, be interchangeable
+through a single selection point, and remain behaviorally compatible. The existing
+`features/auth/services` pair is the reference pattern; extend that pattern rather than invent
+a new one. Mock implementations MUST NOT be imported by production code paths except through
+the selection point.
+
+Rationale: interface-backed services enable parallel frontend/backend work, reliable UI state
+testing, and safe replacement of implementations without touching consumers.
+
+### V. DTO and Domain Separation via Explicit Mappers
+
+API DTOs and UI/domain types MUST be defined separately. Transport shapes live in
+`features/<name>/types/*.dto.ts` and mirror the wire contract exactly. Domain and UI types live
+in `features/<name>/types/` and express application meaning, including discriminated unions and
+narrowed role or status models. Conversion between DTOs and domain types MUST happen in explicit
+functions located in `features/<name>/mappers/`. Components and hooks MUST consume domain types,
+never raw DTOs. Inline transformation inside components or services is prohibited.
+
+Rationale: explicit mapping isolates the UI from backend contract churn and makes every
+translation visible, testable, and reviewable.
+
+### VI. Token-Based Design System and Component Layering
+
+Colors MUST NOT be hardcoded in components, styles, or inline props. All colors MUST be declared
+as design tokens in `src/app/globals.css` (CSS custom properties exposed through the Tailwind
+`@theme` layer) and consumed as token-backed utilities or variables. New tokens MUST be added to
+the token layer instead of introducing one-off values. Generic, reusable UI primitives MUST live
+in `src/components/ui`. Shared layout and structural chrome (headers, shells, navigation frames)
+MUST live in `src/components/layout`. Existing specialized groups such as `src/components/forms`
+and `src/components/icons` remain valid for their scope and MUST NOT be duplicated into `ui`.
+Feature-specific components stay inside their feature.
+
+Rationale: a single token source and clear component layers keep the interface visually
+consistent, themeable, and free of duplicated primitives.
+
+### VII. Explicit Data States in Every Data-Driven Section
+
+Every data-driven section MUST explicitly implement and render four states: loading, empty,
+error, and success. Loading MUST use a stable placeholder that preserves layout; empty MUST
+explain that no data exists and offer a next step when applicable; error MUST present a
+human-readable message and a recovery action; success MUST render the data. Silent failures,
+indefinite spinners, and unhandled rejected promises are prohibited in UI code.
+
+Rationale: explicit states make the interface trustworthy under real network conditions and
+force failure handling to be designed rather than discovered in production.
+
+### VIII. Accessibility and Separation of Concerns (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
+
+Accessibility is mandatory. All interactive elements MUST be reachable and operable by keyboard,
+MUST expose accessible names, MUST show visible focus, and MUST use semantic HTML before ARIA.
+Forms MUST associate labels, descriptions, and validation errors with their inputs. Contrast MUST
+meet WCAG 2.1 AA using design tokens. UI rendering MUST use React function components and hooks;
+class components are prohibited. Service and domain logic SHOULD use object-oriented design where
+it improves encapsulation, invariants, and dependency inversion, while remaining free of React
+dependencies. Components MUST NOT own transport, mapping, or business rules.
+
+Rationale: accessibility is a correctness requirement, and separating rendering from service and
+domain logic keeps each layer independently understandable and replaceable.
+
+## Additional Constraints
+
+Technology and repository constraints are non-negotiable unless this constitution is amended.
+
+- **Approved stack**: Next.js App Router, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, React Hook Form,
+  Zod, and the existing session/auth libraries. Prefer platform and existing-library
+  capabilities over new packages.
+- **Dependencies**: A new runtime dependency MUST be justified in the change description with the
+  problem it solves and why existing code or platform APIs are insufficient. Dependencies without
+  justification MUST NOT be merged.
+- **Inspect before introducing**: Contributors MUST inspect the existing codebase before adding a
+  convention, component, hook, or utility. Equivalent existing implementations MUST be reused or
+  extended.
+- **No unnecessary duplication**: Parallel implementations of the same behavior MUST NOT be
+  created. If an existing pattern is insufficient, improve it in place and migrate callers.
+- **No unnecessary restructuring**: Existing structure MUST NOT be reorganized for preference
+  alone. Restructuring requires a concrete maintenance or correctness justification.
+- **Route and boundary integrity**: Server-only modules MUST NOT be imported into client
+  components. Secrets and server configuration MUST never reach client bundles.
+- **Scope discipline**: Features MUST implement only agreed requirements; speculative abstraction
+  and unused extension points MUST be avoided.
+
+## Development Workflow and Quality Gates
+
+- Before requesting review, contributors MUST run `npm run lint` and `npm run build`, and MUST
+  resolve all new errors and warnings.
+- If a dedicated typecheck script exists, it MUST pass; otherwise `npm run build` is the type
+  gate.
+- Every pull request and review MUST verify compliance with this constitution, including feature
+  layout, API client usage, mock parity, mapper boundaries, token usage, the four data states,
+  and accessibility.
+- A principle violation MUST be fixed or documented as an explicit, time-bound exception approved
+  by maintainers in the change description.
+- New features MUST ship with their mock service implementation so the feature is usable without a
+  live backend.
+- Reviewers MUST block changes that introduce hardcoded colors, direct network calls, DTO leakage
+  into components, or inaccessible interactive elements.
+- `AGENTS.md` provides agent-facing instructions and `DEV_NOTES.md` records working technical
+  decisions; neither overrides this constitution.
+
 ## Governance
-<!-- Example: Constitution supersedes all other practices; Amendments require documentation, approval, migration plan -->
 
-[GOVERNANCE_RULES]
-<!-- Example: All PRs/reviews must verify compliance; Complexity must be justified; Use [GUIDANCE_FILE] for runtime development guidance -->
+This constitution supersedes conflicting local conventions and preferences. When a conflict is
+discovered, the constitution governs until it is formally amended.
 
-**Version**: [CONSTITUTION_VERSION] | **Ratified**: [RATIFICATION_DATE] | **Last Amended**: [LAST_AMENDED_DATE]
-<!-- Example: Version: 2.1.1 | Ratified: 2025-06-13 | Last Amended: 2025-07-16 -->
+Amendments require a written proposal describing the change, its rationale, the affected
+principles or sections, and the migration impact on existing code. Amendments MUST be reviewed and
+approved by project maintainers before merge. The amendment MUST update the version, the
+`Last Amended` date, and remove the temporary Sync Impact Report before commit.
+
+Versioning follows semantic versioning. MAJOR increments require backward-incompatible governance
+changes, such as removing or redefining a principle. MINOR increments require a new principle or
+section, or materially expanded guidance. PATCH increments cover clarifications, wording, and
+non-semantic refinements.
+
+Compliance review is mandatory for every change. Maintainers MUST verify the principles during
+review and MAY request changes solely on constitutional grounds. Repeated non-compliance MUST be
+addressed through documentation, review guidance, or an explicit amendment rather than tolerated.
+
+**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-11-13 | **Last Amended**: 2026-11-13

## User Input

```text
/speckit.constitution

Establish engineering principles for the myHCMUS frontend.

Core principles:
- Use Next.js App Router and TypeScript.
- Follow a feature-first architecture:
  features/<name>/{components,hooks,services,types,mappers}.
- All HTTP communication must go through libs/api-client.ts.
- Each feature service must have a mock implementation behind the
  same interface, following the existing authentication feature pattern.
- Keep API DTOs and UI/domain types separate, using explicit mappers.
- Generic UI components belong in components/ui.
- Shared layout components belong in components/layout.
- Do not hardcode colors. Use design tokens defined in globals.css.
- Every data-driven section must handle loading, empty, error,
  and success states.
- Accessibility is mandatory.
- Prefer reusable, maintainable components and clear separation
  of concerns.
- Apply OOP principles to service and domain logic where appropriate.
  Use React functional components and hooks for UI rendering.

Repository constraints:
- Inspect the existing codebase before introducing new conventions.
- Reuse existing implementations and patterns whenever appropriate.
- Do not unnecessarily duplicate or restructure existing code.
- Do not introduce dependencies without justification. 
```

You **MUST** consider the user input before proceeding (if not empty).

## Scope Guard

This command's own work is limited to updating the project constitution itself. Dependent templates
and commands read the constitution at runtime and are not modified here.

- Classify every part of the user input as either constitution content or a separate,
  non-governance intent.
- If the input includes feature implementation, code generation, refactoring, building, or
  deployment requests, you **MUST NOT** execute them. Extract them as deferred intents instead.
- You **MUST NOT** create, modify, or delete application source files, feature routes,
  components, tests, deployment files, or other artifacts unrelated to the constitution
  workflow.
- If it is unclear whether an instruction is constitution content, ask for clarification before
  making changes.
- After completing the constitution update, include a `Next Actions` section for each deferred
  intent. List the original intent and suggest the appropriate follow-up Spec Kit command, such
  as `/speckit.specify`, without invoking it.
- If there are no non-governance intents, omit the `Next Actions` section.

## Pre-Execution Checks

**Check for extension hooks (before constitution update)**:
- Check if `.specify/extensions.yml` exists in the project root.
- If it exists, read it and look for entries under the `hooks.before_constitution` key
- If the YAML cannot be parsed or is invalid, do not skip silently: tell the user that `.specify/extensions.yml` could not be read (include the parser error) and that no hooks were checked, including any mandatory (`optional: false`) hooks registered there, then continue normally
- Filter out hooks where `enabled` is explicitly `false`. Treat hooks without an `enabled` field as enabled by default.
- For each remaining hook, do **not** attempt to interpret or evaluate hook `condition` expressions:
  - If the hook has no `condition` field, or it is null/empty, treat the hook as executable
  - If the hook defines a non-empty `condition`, skip the hook and leave condition evaluation to the HookExecutor implementation
- For each executable hook, output the following based on its `optional` flag:
  - **Optional hook** (`optional: true`):
    ```
    ## Extension Hooks

    **Optional Pre-Hook**: {extension}
    Command: `/{command}`
    Description: {description}

    Prompt: {prompt}
    To execute: `/{command}`
    ```
  - **Mandatory hook** (`optional: false`):
    ```
    ## Extension Hooks

    **Automatic Pre-Hook**: {extension}
    Executing: `/{command}`
    EXECUTE_COMMAND: {command}

    Wait for the result of the hook command before proceeding to the Outline.
    ```
    After emitting the block above you MUST actually invoke the hook and wait for it to finish before continuing. Run it the same way you would run the command yourself in this agent/session (the invocation may differ from the literal `{command}` id shown above, e.g. a skills-mode agent runs it as `/skill:speckit-...` or `$speckit-...`). Emitting the block alone does not run the hook.
- If no hooks are registered or `.specify/extensions.yml` does not exist, skip silently

## Outline

You are updating the project constitution at `.specify/memory/constitution.md`. The active
constitution scaffold is resolved at command time from `constitution-template` through the Spec Kit
preset/template resolution stack.

Follow this execution flow:

1. Run `.specify/scripts/powershell/resolve-template.ps1 constitution-template -Json` from the repository root and parse `TEMPLATE_CONTENT` as the active template.
   - The shared resolver applies project overrides, composing preset layers, and extension layers
     before the core template fallback. It MUST succeed before continuing.
   - If it fails, stop and report the resolution error; do not continue with only one contributing
     template layer.
   - If `.specify/memory/constitution.md` exists, load it as the source of current project-specific
     values and amendments. Preserve information that is still applicable when applying the newly
     resolved scaffold.
   - If it does not exist, use the resolved template as the initial document.
   - Do not write back to any versioned template layer.
   - Identify every placeholder token of the form `[ALL_CAPS_IDENTIFIER]`.
   **IMPORTANT**: The user might require less or more principles than the ones used in the template. If a number is specified, respect that - follow the general template. You will update the doc accordingly.

2. Collect/derive values for placeholders:
   - If user input (conversation) supplies a value, use it.
   - Otherwise infer from existing repo context (README, docs, prior constitution versions if embedded).
   - For governance dates: `RATIFICATION_DATE` is the original adoption date (if unknown ask or mark TODO), `LAST_AMENDED_DATE` is today if changes are made, otherwise keep previous.
   - `CONSTITUTION_VERSION` must increment according to semantic versioning rules:
     - MAJOR: Backward incompatible governance/principle removals or redefinitions.
     - MINOR: New principle/section added or materially expanded guidance.
     - PATCH: Clarifications, wording, typo fixes, non-semantic refinements.
   - If version bump type ambiguous, propose reasoning before finalizing.

3. Draft the updated constitution content using the resolved template as the required structure:
   - Replace every placeholder with concrete text (no bracketed tokens left except intentionally retained template slots that the project has chosen not to define yetΓÇöexplicitly justify any left).
   - Preserve heading hierarchy and comments can be removed once replaced unless they still add clarifying guidance.
   - Ensure each Principle section: succinct name line, paragraph (or bullet list) capturing nonΓÇænegotiable rules, explicit rationale if not obvious.
   - Ensure Governance section lists amendment procedure, versioning policy, and compliance review expectations.

4. Produce a Sync Impact Report as an HTML comment at the top of the constitution file after update.
   This report is temporary scratch material for human review of the amendment, not governance
   content; it is expected to be removed before the amended constitution file is committed.
   - Version change: old ΓåÆ new
   - List of modified principles (old title ΓåÆ new title if renamed)
   - Added sections
   - Removed sections
   - Follow-up TODOs if any placeholders intentionally deferred.

5. Validation before final output:
   - No remaining unexplained bracket tokens.
   - Version line matches report.
   - Dates ISO format YYYY-MM-DD.
   - Principles are declarative, testable, and free of vague language ("should" ΓåÆ replace with MUST/SHOULD rationale where appropriate).

6. Write the completed constitution back to `.specify/memory/constitution.md` (overwrite).

7. Output a final summary to the user with:
   - New version and bump rationale.
   - Any TODO placeholders or deferred items requiring manual follow-up.
   - Suggested commit message (e.g., `docs: amend constitution to vX.Y.Z (principle additions + governance update)`).
   - A `Next Actions` section for any deferred non-governance intents.

Formatting & Style Requirements:

- Use Markdown headings exactly as in the template (do not demote/promote levels).
- Wrap long rationale lines to keep readability (<100 chars ideally) but do not hard enforce with awkward breaks.
- Keep a single blank line between sections.
- Avoid trailing whitespace.

If the user supplies partial updates (e.g., only one principle revision), still perform validation and version decision steps.

If critical info missing (e.g., ratification date truly unknown), insert `TODO(<FIELD_NAME>): explanation` and include in the Sync Impact Report under deferred items.

Write only `.specify/memory/constitution.md`; do not create or modify template source files.

## Post-Execution Checks

**Check for extension hooks (after constitution update)**:
Check if `.specify/extensions.yml` exists in the project root.
- If it exists, read it and look for entries under the `hooks.after_constitution` key
- If the YAML cannot be parsed or is invalid, do not skip silently: tell the user that `.specify/extensions.yml` could not be read (include the parser error) and that no hooks were checked, including any mandatory (`optional: false`) hooks registered there, then continue normally
- Filter out hooks where `enabled` is explicitly `false`. Treat hooks without an `enabled` field as enabled by default.
- For each remaining hook, do **not** attempt to interpret or evaluate hook `condition` expressions:
  - If the hook has no `condition` field, or it is null/empty, treat the hook as executable
  - If the hook defines a non-empty `condition`, skip the hook and leave condition evaluation to the HookExecutor implementation
- For each executable hook, output the following based on its `optional` flag:
  - **Optional hook** (`optional: true`):
    ```
    ## Extension Hooks

    **Optional Hook**: {extension}
    Command: `/{command}`
    Description: {description}

    Prompt: {prompt}
    To execute: `/{command}`
    ```
  - **Mandatory hook** (`optional: false`):
    ```
    ## Extension Hooks

    **Automatic Hook**: {extension}
    Executing: `/{command}`
    EXECUTE_COMMAND: {command}
    ```
    After emitting the block above you MUST actually invoke the hook and wait for it to finish before continuing. Run it the same way you would run the command yourself in this agent/session (the invocation may differ from the literal `{command}` id shown above, e.g. a skills-mode agent runs it as `/skill:speckit-...` or `$speckit-...`). Emitting the block alone does not run the hook.
- If no hooks are registered or `.specify/extensions.yml` does not exist, skip silently

and route grouping such as `(public)` and `(protected)` MUST be preserved. Strict type safety is
mandatory: no `any` in new production code, no type assertions used to bypass validation, and no
JavaScript source files for application logic. Server Components MUST be the default; `"use client"`
is added only when interactivity, browser APIs, or client-only hooks require it.

Rationale: the App Router and TypeScript are the project's established foundation, and their
consistent use keeps routing, rendering, and data boundaries predictable.

### II. Feature-First Architecture (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

Business capabilities MUST be organized as self-contained features under
`src/features/<name>/` with the internal structure `components/`, `hooks/`, `services/`,
`types/`, and `mappers/`, creating each directory only when the feature needs it. Feature code
MUST NOT import another feature's internals directly; cross-feature reuse happens through shared
modules in `src/libs`, `src/components`, or `src/types`. Application routes remain thin and MUST
delegate behavior to feature modules.

Rationale: feature isolation limits coupling, makes ownership clear, and prevents the application
from collapsing into a shared pile of unrelated modules.

### III. Centralized HTTP Through the API Client (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

All HTTP communication MUST go through `src/libs/api-client.ts` (imported as `@/libs/api-client`).
Direct use of `fetch`, `axios`, `XMLHttpRequest`, or any other transport outside that module is
prohibited. Features MUST NOT construct base URLs; the API client owns base URL resolution,
headers, serialization, and error normalization. New transport behavior MUST be added to the
shared API client rather than reimplemented per feature.

Rationale: one transport boundary guarantees consistent authentication, error handling, and
observability, and prevents divergent network behavior across features.

### IV. Service Contracts with Paired Mock Implementations (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

Every feature MUST expose its data operations through a service contract: a TypeScript
`interface` in `features/<name>/services/`. Each contract MUST have two implementations: a real
implementation that calls the API client, and a mock implementation that returns deterministic
fixtures with simulated latency. Both MUST implement the same interface, be interchangeable
through a single selection point, and remain behaviorally compatible. The existing
`features/auth/services` pair is the reference pattern; extend that pattern rather than invent
a new one. Mock implementations MUST NOT be imported by production code paths except through
the selection point.

Rationale: interface-backed services enable parallel frontend/backend work, reliable UI state
testing, and safe replacement of implementations without touching consumers.

### V. DTO and Domain Separation via Explicit Mappers

API DTOs and UI/domain types MUST be defined separately. Transport shapes live in
`features/<name>/types/*.dto.ts` and mirror the wire contract exactly. Domain and UI types live
in `features/<name>/types/` and express application meaning, including discriminated unions and
narrowed role or status models. Conversion between DTOs and domain types MUST happen in explicit
functions located in `features/<name>/mappers/`. Components and hooks MUST consume domain types,
never raw DTOs. Inline transformation inside components or services is prohibited.

Rationale: explicit mapping isolates the UI from backend contract churn and makes every
translation visible, testable, and reviewable.

### VI. Token-Based Design System and Component Layering

Colors MUST NOT be hardcoded in components, styles, or inline props. All colors MUST be declared
as design tokens in `src/app/globals.css` (CSS custom properties exposed through the Tailwind
`@theme` layer) and consumed as token-backed utilities or variables. New tokens MUST be added to
the token layer instead of introducing one-off values. Generic, reusable UI primitives MUST live
in `src/components/ui`. Shared layout and structural chrome (headers, shells, navigation frames)
MUST live in `src/components/layout`. Existing specialized groups such as `src/components/forms`
and `src/components/icons` remain valid for their scope and MUST NOT be duplicated into `ui`.
Feature-specific components stay inside their feature.

Rationale: a single token source and clear component layers keep the interface visually
consistent, themeable, and free of duplicated primitives.

### VII. Explicit Data States in Every Data-Driven Section

Every data-driven section MUST explicitly implement and render four states: loading, empty,
error, and success. Loading MUST use a stable placeholder that preserves layout; empty MUST
explain that no data exists and offer a next step when applicable; error MUST present a
human-readable message and a recovery action; success MUST render the data. Silent failures,
indefinite spinners, and unhandled rejected promises are prohibited in UI code.

Rationale: explicit states make the interface trustworthy under real network conditions and
force failure handling to be designed rather than discovered in production.

### VIII. Accessibility and Separation of Concerns (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

Accessibility is mandatory. All interactive elements MUST be reachable and operable by keyboard,
MUST expose accessible names, MUST show visible focus, and MUST use semantic HTML before ARIA.
Forms MUST associate labels, descriptions, and validation errors with their inputs. Contrast MUST
meet WCAG 2.1 AA using design tokens. UI rendering MUST use React function components and hooks;
class components are prohibited. Service and domain logic SHOULD use object-oriented design where
it improves encapsulation, invariants, and dependency inversion, while remaining free of React
dependencies. Components MUST NOT own transport, mapping, or business rules.

Rationale: accessibility is a correctness requirement, and separating rendering from service and
domain logic keeps each layer independently understandable and replaceable.

## Additional Constraints

Technology and repository constraints are non-negotiable unless this constitution is amended.

- **Approved stack**: Next.js App Router, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, React Hook Form,
  Zod, and the existing session/auth libraries. Prefer platform and existing-library
  capabilities over new packages.
- **Dependencies**: A new runtime dependency MUST be justified in the change description with the
  problem it solves and why existing code or platform APIs are insufficient. Dependencies without
  justification MUST NOT be merged.
- **Inspect before introducing**: Contributors MUST inspect the existing codebase before adding a
  convention, component, hook, or utility. Equivalent existing implementations MUST be reused or
  extended.
- **No unnecessary duplication**: Parallel implementations of the same behavior MUST NOT be
  created. If an existing pattern is insufficient, improve it in place and migrate callers.
- **No unnecessary restructuring**: Existing structure MUST NOT be reorganized for preference
  alone. Restructuring requires a concrete maintenance or correctness justification.
- **Route and boundary integrity**: Server-only modules MUST NOT be imported into client
  components. Secrets and server configuration MUST never reach client bundles.
- **Scope discipline**: Features MUST implement only agreed requirements; speculative abstraction
  and unused extension points MUST be avoided.

## Development Workflow and Quality Gates

- Before requesting review, contributors MUST run `npm run lint` and `npm run build`, and MUST
  resolve all new errors and warnings.
- If a dedicated typecheck script exists, it MUST pass; otherwise `npm run build` is the type
  gate.
- Every pull request and review MUST verify compliance with this constitution, including feature
  layout, API client usage, mock parity, mapper boundaries, token usage, the four data states,
  and accessibility.
- A principle violation MUST be fixed or documented as an explicit, time-bound exception approved
  by maintainers in the change description.
- New features MUST ship with their mock service implementation so the feature is usable without a
  live backend.
- Reviewers MUST block changes that introduce hardcoded colors, direct network calls, DTO leakage
  into components, or inaccessible interactive elements.
- `AGENTS.md` provides agent-facing instructions and `DEV_NOTES.md` records working technical
  decisions; neither overrides this constitution.

## Governance

This constitution supersedes conflicting local conventions and preferences. When a conflict is
discovered, the constitution governs until it is formally amended.

Amendments require a written proposal describing the change, its rationale, the affected
principles or sections, and the migration impact on existing code. Amendments MUST be reviewed and
approved by project maintainers before merge. The amendment MUST update the version, the
`Last Amended` date, and remove the temporary Sync Impact Report before commit.

Versioning follows semantic versioning. MAJOR increments require backward-incompatible governance
changes, such as removing or redefining a principle. MINOR increments require a new principle or
section, or materially expanded guidance. PATCH increments cover clarifications, wording, and
non-semantic refinements.

Compliance review is mandatory for every change. Maintainers MUST verify the principles during
review and MAY request changes solely on constitutional grounds. Repeated non-compliance MUST be
addressed through documentation, review guidance, or an explicit amendment rather than tolerated.

@@ -0,0 +1,286 @@
+# Feature Specification: Public Landing Page
+
+**Feature Branch**: `001-landing-page`
+
+**Created**: 2026-11-13
+
+**Status**: Draft
+
+**Input**: User description: "Build the public Landing Page at route '/'. Read docs/spec/landing-page-spec.md, especially sections 1, 2, 7, and 8, as the primary source of requirements. Implement the six Landing Page sections; define user-facing behavior and interactions; describe navigation and user flows; specify activity discovery behavior; define loading, empty, error, and success states; include responsive behavior and accessibility requirements. Frontend-only feature; backend handled by a separate team; do not assume proposed API contracts are confirmed; identify unclear requirements and assumptions explicitly; do not invent additional product features."
+
+## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
+
+### User Story 1 - Guest discovers the platform and activities (Priority: P1)
+
+A first-time visitor opens the public home page, immediately understands what myHCMUS offers, sees featured and upcoming activities, and can choose to sign in, jump to the activity section, or continue exploring the page.
+
+**Why this priority**: This is the primary public entry point and the main value of the feature. Without it there is no landing experience at all.
+
+**Independent Test**: Load the home page as a signed-out visitor with activity content available and verify that all six sections render, up to two featured and three compact activities appear, the header shows a sign-in action, and both hero actions behave as described.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** a signed-out visitor opens the home page, **When** the page loads, **Then** the header, hero, platform highlights, help, and footer are visible immediately while the activity area shows loading placeholders.
+2. **Given** activity content becomes available, **When** loading completes, **Then** at most two featured activities and at most three compact activities are shown with image, title, categories, date and time, location, and registration status where applicable.
+3. **Given** a signed-out visitor activates "Get Started", **When** the action completes, **Then** the sign-in experience opens with the visitor's intended return destination preserved.
+4. **Given** a signed-out visitor activates "Explore the activities", **When** the action completes, **Then** the view moves to the activity section and the address reflects that section.
+5. **Given** the visitor selects an activity card, **When** the action completes, **Then** the corresponding activity detail destination opens.
+
+---
+
+### User Story 2 - Activity discovery remains clear in every outcome (Priority: P2)
+
+A visitor encounters slow, empty, partial, or failed activity content and still receives a clear, honest explanation with a way forward, while the rest of the page remains usable.
+
+**Why this priority**: Activity discovery depends on an external data source. Trustworthy handling of every outcome is required for the landing page to be usable in real conditions.
+
+**Independent Test**: Drive the activity area through loading, populated, empty, partial, and failed outcomes using controlled test content, and verify the rendered message, layout adaptation, and retry behavior for each.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** the activity content is still loading, **When** the visitor views the section, **Then** placeholders match the final layout footprint and the area is announced as busy without shifting the page.
+2. **Given** the data source returns no activities, **When** loading completes, **Then** an empty message explains that new activities will appear and no empty grid is shown.
+3. **Given** the data source fails, **When** loading completes, **Then** an error message and a "Try again" action appear while every other section remains fully usable.
+4. **Given** the visitor activates "Try again", **When** retry starts, **Then** the section returns to its loading presentation and ends in a success, empty, or error outcome.
+5. **Given** only featured activities exist, **When** content renders, **Then** featured cards occupy the available width without leaving an empty column.
+6. **Given** only upcoming activities exist, **When** content renders, **Then** those activities are shown in the featured card presentation.
+
+---
+
+### User Story 3 - Guest sees which services require sign-in (Priority: P3)
+
+A signed-out visitor can use the publicly available university services, clearly understands that other services require an account, and is invited to sign in to unlock them.
+
+**Why this priority**: Services are a core promise of the platform, and the locked presentation is the main conversion path from the landing page.
+
+**Independent Test**: Load the services section as a signed-out visitor and verify public services are usable, protected services are obscured and unreachable, and the sign-in invitation leads to the sign-in experience.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** a signed-out visitor views the services area, **When** it renders, **Then** publicly available services are fully visible and usable.
+2. **Given** a signed-out visitor views a protected service, **When** it renders, **Then** it is visibly obscured, cannot be focused, activated, selected, or announced by assistive technology, and exposes no destination.
+3. **Given** a signed-out visitor activates the sign-in invitation over the protected services, **When** the action completes, **Then** the sign-in experience opens with a return destination that leads back to the services area.
+4. **Given** authentication is still resolving, **When** the services area renders, **Then** it shows the locked presentation until the visitor's status is known, with no layout shift when it unlocks.
+
+---
+
+### User Story 4 - Signed-in visitor keeps using the landing page (Priority: P4)
+
+A signed-in student, organizer, or administrator can still visit the public landing page, sees a direct path to their dashboard, and finds every service unlocked.
+
+**Why this priority**: Signed-in visitors must not be redirected away or lose access to public content, and they must be able to return to their work quickly.
+
+**Independent Test**: Load the landing page as each signed-in role and verify no forced redirect occurs, the header reports the correct dashboard destination, and all services are usable.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** a signed-in visitor opens the home page, **When** the page loads, **Then** the landing page remains visible and no automatic redirect occurs.
+2. **Given** a signed-in visitor views the header, **When** it renders, **Then** a "Dashboard" action is present and leads to the dashboard appropriate to that visitor's role.
+3. **Given** a signed-in visitor views the services area, **When** it renders, **Then** every service is fully visible and usable.
+4. **Given** a signed-in visitor activates "Get Started", **When** the action completes, **Then** the destination is the dashboard appropriate to that visitor's role.
+
+---
+
+### User Story 5 - Visitors navigate the page predictably (Priority: P5)
+
+A visitor uses the header to move between sections, always knows which section is in view, and can navigate comfortably on a small screen or with a keyboard.
+
+**Why this priority**: Navigation makes the long single-page experience usable and accessible, but the page still delivers value without perfect navigation polish.
+
+**Independent Test**: Use header links, direct section addresses, the mobile menu, and keyboard-only navigation to reach every section and verify positioning, active indication, and focus behavior.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** a visitor selects a header link, **When** the action completes, **Then** the matching section is positioned below the floating header and the address reflects the section.
+2. **Given** a visitor scrolls through the page, **When** a new section becomes the main section in view, **Then** the matching header link is indicated as active by more than color alone.
+3. **Given** a visitor opens a direct section address, **When** the page loads, **Then** the target section is positioned below the floating header.
+4. **Given** a visitor on a narrow screen opens the header menu, **When** it opens, **Then** all section links and the authentication action are available, keyboard focus is managed, and the menu can be dismissed predictably.
+
+---
+
+### Edge Cases
+
+- Activity content arrives slowly: placeholders persist without a timeout error and without blocking the rest of the page.
+- Activity content arrives after the visitor has left the section or page: no visible error or stale update occurs.
+- Activity content is malformed, incomplete, or contains an unreadable date: the activity area shows the error outcome rather than broken cards.
+- An activity title is very long: featured titles are limited to four lines and compact titles to three lines, with an ellipsis.
+- An activity spans multiple days: the date and time presentation clearly shows both the start and end dates.
+- An activity has no cover image or the image fails: a branded placeholder appears without changing card dimensions.
+- An activity has no categories or no location: the corresponding line is omitted rather than showing empty punctuation.
+- The hero visual fails: the hero keeps its layout and text remains readable over a solid fallback.
+- The visitor's sign-in status cannot be resolved: the services area remains in the locked presentation and no protected destination is exposed.
+- Only four of the six planned services are confirmed: the services area remains usable and no service is invented to fill the grid.
+- A guide destination is not yet available: the card must not ship as a dead link; the destination is resolved or the card is presented as unavailable before release.
+- The visitor requests reduced motion: section navigation is immediate and hover lift effects are not required.
+- The viewport is 320 pixels wide: no horizontal scrolling occurs and all actions remain reachable.
+- The visitor activates retry repeatedly: the area settles in one outcome without duplicate content or conflicting messages.
+- A section address is opened before fonts and images finish loading: the target section is still positioned correctly.
+
+## Requirements *(mandatory)*
+
+### Functional Requirements
+
+**Landing composition and access**
+
+- **FR-001**: The home page MUST be publicly accessible to signed-out and signed-in visitors, with no forced redirect for signed-in visitors.
+- **FR-002**: The page MUST present six content sections in this order: Hero, Platform Highlights, Featured and Upcoming Activities, HCMUS Services, Help and Guide, and Footer. A global header MUST float over the hero.
+- **FR-003**: Each section MUST have a stable, shareable section address: home, about, activities, services, help, and contact.
+- **FR-004**: A failure in activity discovery MUST NOT disable, hide, or degrade any other section.
+
+**Header and navigation**
+
+- **FR-005**: The header MUST show the myHCMUS brand, section links for Home, About Us, Activities, Services, and Help, and an authentication action.
+- **FR-006**: The brand MUST return the visitor to the top of the landing page.
+- **FR-007**: A signed-out visitor MUST see a "Log In" action that opens the sign-in experience and preserves the visitor's intended return destination.
+- **FR-008**: A signed-in visitor MUST see a "Dashboard" action that opens the dashboard appropriate to that visitor's role.
+- **FR-009**: While sign-in status is resolving, the header MUST reserve stable space for the authentication action and MUST NOT briefly show a signed-in-only action.
+- **FR-010**: Selecting a section link MUST move the view smoothly to that section, offset for the floating header, and update the address to reflect the section.
+- **FR-011**: The header MUST indicate the section currently in view, using a cue in addition to color.
+- **FR-012**: Opening a direct section address MUST position the target section below the floating header.
+- **FR-013**: On viewports below 1024 pixels wide, the primary section links MUST collapse into a menu control. The opened menu MUST contain the same links and authentication action, be operable by keyboard, manage focus, and close predictably.
+
+**Hero**
+
+- **FR-014**: The hero MUST show the headline, supporting subtitle, a campus visual, and two actions: "Get Started" and "Explore the activities".
+- **FR-015**: "Get Started" MUST open the sign-in experience for a signed-out visitor and the role-appropriate dashboard for a signed-in visitor.
+- **FR-016**: "Explore the activities" MUST move the visitor to the activity section. The destination MUST remain a single configurable value so it can later point to a dedicated activity listing.
+- **FR-017**: If the hero visual cannot be displayed, the hero MUST keep its layout and keep all text readable over a fallback background.
+
+**Platform Highlights**
+
+- **FR-018**: The highlights section MUST present exactly three highlights, each with an image, title, and description.
+- **FR-019**: Highlights MUST be informational only and MUST NOT be presented as links.
+
+**Featured and Upcoming Activities**
+
+- **FR-020**: The activity section header MUST remain visible in every activity outcome.
+- **FR-021**: Activity discovery MUST NOT block the first presentation of the rest of the page.
+- **FR-022**: While activity content is loading, the section MUST show placeholders that match the final footprint of two featured cards and three compact cards, with no layout shift when content appears.
+- **FR-023**: Loading activity content MUST be announced to assistive technology as a busy, updating area.
+- **FR-024**: On success, the section MUST show at most two featured activities and at most three compact activities; any additional items MUST be ignored.
+- **FR-025**: When both featured and upcoming activities exist, featured cards MUST occupy the left area and compact cards MUST be stacked to the right.
+- **FR-026**: When featured activities exist and no upcoming activities exist, featured cards MUST span the available width without an empty second column.
+- **FR-027**: When no featured activities exist and upcoming activities exist, the upcoming activities MUST be presented in the featured card style, up to three columns.
+- **FR-028**: When no activities exist at all, the section MUST show the empty outcome and MUST NOT show an empty grid.
+- **FR-029**: A featured activity card MUST show a cover image, the title exactly as supplied, categories, date and time, location, registration status, and a "View" affordance.
+- **FR-030**: A compact activity card MUST show a thumbnail, the title exactly as supplied, a category label, date and time, and location, without a registration status.
+- **FR-031**: Featured activity titles MUST be limited to four lines and compact titles to three lines, with an ellipsis when truncated.
+- **FR-032**: Registration status MUST map to the labels "Registration Open", "Registration Upcoming", and "Registration Closed", each with a visible text label and a non-color-only indicator.
+- **FR-033**: The whole activity card MUST be a single link to that activity's detail destination; the "View" affordance MUST NOT be a separate link.
+- **FR-034**: Activity date and time MUST be shown in 24-hour format as day/month/year and hour:minute, using the Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh timezone. A multi-day activity MUST show both start and end dates.
+- **FR-035**: A missing or failed activity image MUST be replaced by a branded placeholder that preserves card dimensions.
+- **FR-036**: Missing categories or missing location MUST cause the corresponding line to be omitted without leaving empty punctuation.
+- **FR-037**: The empty outcome MUST state that no activities are available right now, explain that new activities will appear once announced, and reserve at least the height of one featured card row.
+- **FR-038**: The error outcome MUST state that activities could not be loaded, advise the visitor to check the connection and try again, and offer a "Try again" action.
+- **FR-039**: "Try again" MUST return the section to the loading presentation and MUST end in exactly one success, empty, or error outcome without duplicate content.
+- **FR-040**: Activity content that is malformed or cannot be interpreted MUST be treated as the error outcome, not rendered as broken cards.
+
+**HCMUS Services**
+
+- **FR-041**: The services section MUST present six service entries arranged in three columns and two rows on wide viewports, each with an icon, name, and "Access" affordance.
+- **FR-042**: Each service entry MUST be marked as either publicly available or requiring sign-in.
+- **FR-043**: A signed-out visitor MUST be able to see and use every publicly available service.
+- **FR-044**: A signed-out visitor MUST see services that require sign-in as visibly obscured, reduced in prominence, non-interactive, unreachable by keyboard, excluded from text selection, and hidden from assistive technology.
+- **FR-045**: The signed-out presentation MUST NOT expose the destination of a service that requires sign-in.
+- **FR-046**: The signed-out presentation MUST include an accessible invitation to sign in over the obscured services, leading to the sign-in experience with a return destination that leads back to the services section.
+- **FR-047**: While sign-in status is resolving, the section MUST show the locked presentation and MUST unlock without layout shift once the visitor is confirmed signed in.
+- **FR-048**: A signed-in visitor MUST see every service fully visible and usable.
+- **FR-049**: Every usable service link MUST have an accessible name and open in a new tab when the destination is external.
+- **FR-050**: When fewer than six services are confirmed, the section MUST remain usable and MUST NOT invent service names, icons, or destinations. The final six entries are a release dependency.
+
+**Help and Guide**
+
+- **FR-051**: The help section MUST present four guide cards in two columns and two rows on wide viewports, each with an uppercase title, a short subtitle, and a trailing arrow.
+- **FR-052**: The whole guide card MUST be one link to its configured guide destination, with a hover cue and a visible keyboard focus indicator.
+- **FR-053**: Guide destinations MUST be configurable in one place. A card whose destination is not yet available MUST NOT ship as a dead link; the destination MUST be confirmed, redirected, or the card presented as unavailable before release.
+
+**Footer**
+
+- **FR-054**: The footer MUST contain a brand area with a one-line description, a contact area, a quick-links area reusing the header section links, and a bottom bar.
+- **FR-055**: The bottom bar MUST show a copyright notice with the current year, derived at presentation time rather than fixed text.
+- **FR-056**: Phone and email contact details MUST be actionable as telephone and email links.
+- **FR-057**: Footer copy MUST be configurable in one place because final wording is still pending.
+
+**Responsive behavior**
+
+- **FR-058**: At 1024 pixels wide and above, the page MUST follow the wide layout: three highlight columns, two featured cards with a stack of three compact cards, a three-by-two service grid, and a two-by-two guide grid.
+- **FR-059**: Between 640 and 1023 pixels wide, content MUST adapt to two-column arrangements where applicable, the header MUST use its menu presentation, and activity cards MUST reflow without clipping.
+- **FR-060**: Below 640 pixels wide, content MUST use a single column, hero actions MUST stack at full width, and compact activity cards MUST keep their horizontal presentation.
+- **FR-061**: The page MUST avoid horizontal scrolling at any width from 320 to 1920 pixels.
+- **FR-062**: Interactive targets MUST be at least 44 by 44 pixels on touch screens, and the header menu and obscured services MUST remain usable at narrow widths.
+
+**Accessibility**
+
+- **FR-063**: The page MUST use semantic landmarks for the header, main content, sections, and footer, with exactly one top-level heading, section titles as second-level headings, and card titles as third-level headings.
+- **FR-064**: Every interactive element MUST be operable by keyboard in a logical order and MUST show a visible focus indicator.
+- **FR-065**: Content images MUST have a meaningful text alternative; purely decorative images and shapes MUST be hidden from assistive technology.
+- **FR-066**: Text and meaningful indicators MUST meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast, including the hero headline over the campus visual and white text over deep blue.
+- **FR-067**: When the visitor requests reduced motion, section navigation MUST be immediate and hover movement MUST be suppressed while state changes remain clear.
+- **FR-068**: Loading, empty, and error outcomes MUST be announced to assistive technology without moving focus unexpectedly.
+- **FR-069**: Obscured services and the opened mobile menu MUST NOT be reachable or announced when they are not available to the visitor.
+- **FR-070**: Status MUST NOT be conveyed by color alone; text labels MUST accompany status indicators.
+
+**Content, performance, and sharing**
+
+- **FR-071**: Visible interface copy MUST be in English. Activity titles and other activity content MUST be preserved as supplied, including Vietnamese text.
+- **FR-072**: Section copy, navigation labels, highlights, services, guides, and footer content MUST each come from a single configurable source rather than being scattered through the presentation.
+- **FR-073**: The landing page MUST expose a page title, description, and social sharing preview for the public home page.
+- **FR-074**: The hero visual MUST be presented as early as practical, while below-the-fold imagery MUST NOT delay the first presentation of the page.
+- **FR-075**: Images and placeholders MUST reserve their dimensions so that content arriving later does not shift the layout.
+
+### Key Entities
+
+- **Visitor**: A person viewing the landing page, either signed out or signed in. Signed-in visitors have a role (student, organizer, or administrator) that determines their dashboard destination.
+- **Activity**: A discoverable extracurricular opportunity with an identifier, title, cover image, categories, start and end time, location, registration status, and detail destination.
+- **Activity Collection**: The featured and upcoming activities returned together for the landing page. The landing page displays at most two featured and three upcoming items.
+- **Navigation Link**: A labeled section destination shown in the header and footer, with an active state based on the section in view.
+- **Highlight**: A static benefit statement with an image, title, and description.
+- **Service Entry**: A university service with an icon, name, destination, and an access level of public or requiring sign-in.
+- **Guide Entry**: A help topic with a title, subtitle, and destination.
+- **Footer Content**: Brand description, contact details, quick links, and copyright information.
+
+## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
+
+### Measurable Outcomes
+
+- **SC-001**: At least 90 percent of first-time visitors in usability testing can state the platform's purpose and locate the sign-in action within 15 seconds of the page becoming visible.
+- **SC-002**: The activity section reaches a terminal outcome (populated, empty, or error) within 3 seconds for at least 95 percent of visits on a 10 Mbps connection, with placeholders shown immediately.
+- **SC-003**: The activity section causes no measurable layout shift when content replaces placeholders.
+- **SC-004**: All four activity outcomes can be reproduced and visually verified using controlled test content before release.
+- **SC-005**: A signed-out visitor can reach and activate zero services that require sign-in, verified across keyboard, pointer, and assistive-technology use.
+- **SC-006**: At least 90 percent of signed-out visitors in usability testing understand, without assistance, that signing in unlocks the obscured services.
+- **SC-007**: A signed-in visitor reaches the dashboard appropriate to their role in one action from the header.
+- **SC-008**: Automated accessibility checks report zero critical violations, and every interactive element is reachable and operable by keyboard alone.
+- **SC-009**: The page remains fully usable with no horizontal scrolling at every width from 320 to 1920 pixels.
+- **SC-010**: A failure in activity discovery leaves 100 percent of the other sections navigable and usable in the same visit.
+- **SC-011**: All confirmed interface text passes contrast checks at WCAG 2.1 AA, including the hero headline and white-on-blue content.
+- **SC-012**: At least 95 percent of visitors can navigate from the header to any section on the first attempt, on both wide and narrow screens.
+
+## Assumptions
+
+- Activity content is supplied by a backend capability owned by a separate team. Its final contract is not confirmed, so this specification defines the required visitor-visible behavior and data meaning rather than any request or response contract. The drafts in the source design document are proposals only.
+- The activity detail destination is publicly viewable; registration is assumed to require sign-in. This must be confirmed with the product owner.
+- The dedicated activity listing and help pages are outside this feature. The hero action currently targets the on-page activity section, and help cards target configured help destinations.
+- The page is English-only. Activity content is displayed exactly as supplied and may be Vietnamese.
+- Sign-in is handled by the existing authentication experience and is outside this feature. The landing page only links to it and reflects its state.
+- Signed-in visitors are identified, and their role determines the dashboard destination. This capability already exists in the product.
+- The two unnamed service entries, final hero wording, and final footer copy are pending product input. The feature must not invent them; the layout must remain usable until they are supplied.
+- The "Log in to see all services" invitation is included because it is recommended in the source design. It may be removed without changing the locked-service behavior.
+- The desktop design is the visual source of truth. The 1024-pixel and 640-pixel breakpoints, two-column intermediate layout, and single-column narrow layout are reasonable defaults inferred from the design and must be validated.
+- Visitors use modern evergreen browsers.
+- External university services are third-party destinations. The landing page only links to them and does not control their availability.
+- Obscuring a protected service is a user-experience cue, not a security control. Protected destinations are not secrets, but they are still not exposed in the signed-out presentation.
+- The current year used in the footer is derived when the page is presented.
+- No additional product features beyond the six sections and their stated interactions are in scope.
+
+## Open Questions
+
+These items do not block specification but must be resolved before release or before the relevant content is published.
+
+1. What are the final names and icons for the two remaining university services?
+2. Should the hero headline read "Grown." as designed or "Grow." as likely intended?
+3. Are the help destinations available at release? If not, should the guide cards be hidden, redirected, or presented as unavailable?
+4. Is the activity detail destination public, and does registration require sign-in?
+5. What is the final footer copy, including contact details and hotlines?
+6. Is the sign-in invitation over the obscured services approved for release?
+7. What is the confirmed activity data contract, including how featured and upcoming activities are distinguished?

## User Input

```text
/speckit.specify

Build the public Landing Page at route "/".

Read @docs/spec/landing-page-spec.md, especially sections 1, 2, 7,
and 8, as the primary source of requirements.

Scope:
- Implement the six Landing Page sections.
- Define user-facing behavior and interactions.
- Describe navigation and user flows.
- Specify activity discovery behavior.
- Define loading, empty, error, and success states.
- Include responsive behavior and accessibility requirements.

Focus on WHAT the user should experience, not HOW the
implementation should be structured.

Constraints:
- This is a frontend-only feature.
- Backend development is handled by a separate team.
- Do not assume proposed API contracts are confirmed.
- Identify unclear requirements and assumptions explicitly.
- Do not invent additional product features. 
```

You **MUST** consider the user input before proceeding (if not empty).

## Pre-Execution Checks

**Check for extension hooks (before specification)**:
- Check if `.specify/extensions.yml` exists in the project root.
- If it exists, read it and look for entries under the `hooks.before_specify` key
- If the YAML cannot be parsed or is invalid, do not skip silently: tell the user that `.specify/extensions.yml` could not be read (include the parser error) and that no hooks were checked, including any mandatory (`optional: false`) hooks registered there, then continue normally
- Filter out hooks where `enabled` is explicitly `false`. Treat hooks without an `enabled` field as enabled by default.
- For each remaining hook, do **not** attempt to interpret or evaluate hook `condition` expressions:
  - If the hook has no `condition` field, or it is null/empty, treat the hook as executable
  - If the hook defines a non-empty `condition`, skip the hook and leave condition evaluation to the HookExecutor implementation
- For each executable hook, output the following based on its `optional` flag:
  - **Optional hook** (`optional: true`):
    ```
    ## Extension Hooks

    **Optional Pre-Hook**: {extension}
    Command: `/{command}`
    Description: {description}

    Prompt: {prompt}
    To execute: `/{command}`
    ```
  - **Mandatory hook** (`optional: false`):
    ```
    ## Extension Hooks

    **Automatic Pre-Hook**: {extension}
    Executing: `/{command}`
    EXECUTE_COMMAND: {command}

    Wait for the result of the hook command before proceeding to the Outline.
    ```
    After emitting the block above you MUST actually invoke the hook and wait for it to finish before continuing. Run it the same way you would run the command yourself in this agent/session (the invocation may differ from the literal `{command}` id shown above, e.g. a skills-mode agent runs it as `/skill:speckit-...` or `$speckit-...`). Emitting the block alone does not run the hook.
- If no hooks are registered or `.specify/extensions.yml` does not exist, skip silently

## Outline

The text the user typed after `/speckit.specify` in the triggering message **is** the feature description. Assume you always have it available in this conversation even if `/speckit.specify

Build the public Landing Page at route "/".

Read @docs/spec/landing-page-spec.md, especially sections 1, 2, 7,
and 8, as the primary source of requirements.

Scope:
- Implement the six Landing Page sections.
- Define user-facing behavior and interactions.
- Describe navigation and user flows.
- Specify activity discovery behavior.
- Define loading, empty, error, and success states.
- Include responsive behavior and accessibility requirements.

Focus on WHAT the user should experience, not HOW the
implementation should be structured.

Constraints:
- This is a frontend-only feature.
- Backend development is handled by a separate team.
- Do not assume proposed API contracts are confirmed.
- Identify unclear requirements and assumptions explicitly.
- Do not invent additional product features. ` appears literally below. Do not ask the user to repeat it unless they provided an empty command.

Given that feature description, do this:

1. **Generate a concise short name** (2-4 words) for the feature:
   - Analyze the feature description and extract the most meaningful keywords
   - Create a 2-4 word short name that captures the essence of the feature
   - Use action-noun format when possible (e.g., "add-user-auth", "fix-payment-bug")
   - Preserve technical terms and acronyms (OAuth2, API, JWT, etc.)
   - Keep it concise but descriptive enough to understand the feature at a glance
   - Examples:
     - "I want to add user authentication" ΓåÆ "user-auth"
     - "Implement OAuth2 integration for the API" ΓåÆ "oauth2-api-integration"
     - "Create a dashboard for analytics" ΓåÆ "analytics-dashboard"
     - "Fix payment processing timeout bug" ΓåÆ "fix-payment-timeout"

2. **Branch creation** (optional, via hook):

   If a `before_specify` hook ran successfully in the Pre-Execution Checks above, it will have created/switched to a git branch and output JSON containing `BRANCH_NAME` and `FEATURE_NUM`. Note these values for reference, but the branch name does **not** dictate the spec directory name.

   If the user explicitly provided `GIT_BRANCH_NAME`, pass it through to the hook so the branch script uses the exact value as the branch name (bypassing all prefix/suffix generation).

3. **Create the spec feature directory**:

   Specs live under the default `specs/` directory unless the user explicitly provides `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY`.

   **Resolution order for `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY`**:
   1. If the user explicitly provided `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY` (e.g., via environment variable, argument, or configuration), use it as-is
   2. Otherwise, auto-generate it under `specs/`:
      - Check `.specify/init-options.json` for `feature_numbering` (preferred) or `branch_numbering` (deprecated, migration only ΓÇö will be removed in a future release)
      - If `"timestamp"`: prefix is `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` (current timestamp)
      - If `"sequential"` or absent: prefix is `NNN` (next available 3-digit number after scanning existing directories in `specs/`)
      - Construct the directory name: `<prefix>-<short-name>` (e.g., `003-user-auth` or `20260319-143022-user-auth`)
      - Set `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY` to `specs/<directory-name>`
      - If `branch_numbering` was used (and `feature_numbering` was absent), emit a one-line warning: "ΓÜá∩╕Å `branch_numbering` in init-options.json is deprecated. Rename to `feature_numbering`."

   **Create the directory and spec file**:
   - `mkdir -p SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY`
   - Resolve the active `spec-template` through the Spec Kit preset/template resolution stack (equivalent to `specify preset resolve spec-template`)
   - Copy the resolved `spec-template` file to `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY/spec.md` as the starting point
   - Set `SPEC_FILE` to `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY/spec.md`
   - Persist the resolved path to `.specify/feature.json`:
     ```json
     {
       "feature_directory": "<resolved feature dir>"
     }
     ```
     Write the actual resolved directory path value (for example, `specs/003-user-auth`), not the literal string `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY`.
     This allows downstream commands (`/speckit.plan`, `/speckit.tasks`, etc.) to locate the feature directory without relying on git branch name conventions.

   **IMPORTANT**:
   - You must only create one feature per `/speckit.specify` invocation
   - The spec directory name and the git branch name are independent ΓÇö they may be the same but that is the user's choice
   - The spec directory and file are always created by this command, never by the hook

4. Load the resolved active `spec-template` file to understand required sections.

5. **IF EXISTS**: Load `.specify/memory/constitution.md` for project principles and governance constraints.

6. Follow this execution flow:
    1. Parse user description from arguments
       If empty: ERROR "No feature description provided"
    2. Extract key concepts from description
       Identify: actors, actions, data, constraints
    3. For unclear aspects:
       - Make informed guesses based on context and industry standards
       - Only mark with [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: specific question] if:
         - The choice significantly impacts feature scope or user experience
         - Multiple reasonable interpretations exist with different implications
         - No reasonable default exists
       - **LIMIT: Maximum 3 [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers total**
       - Prioritize clarifications by impact: scope > security/privacy > user experience > technical details
    4. Fill User Scenarios & Testing section
       If no clear user flow: ERROR "Cannot determine user scenarios"
    5. Generate Functional Requirements
       Each requirement must be testable
       Use reasonable defaults for unspecified details (document assumptions in Assumptions section)
    6. Define Success Criteria
       Create measurable, technology-agnostic outcomes
       Include both quantitative metrics (time, performance, volume) and qualitative measures (user satisfaction, task completion)
       Each criterion must be verifiable without implementation details
    7. Identify Key Entities (if data involved)
    8. Return: SUCCESS (spec ready for planning)

7. Write the specification to SPEC_FILE using the template structure, replacing placeholders with concrete details derived from the feature description (arguments) while preserving section order and headings.

8. **Specification Quality Validation**: After writing the initial spec, validate it against quality criteria:

   a. **Create Spec Quality Checklist**: Generate a checklist file at `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY/checklists/requirements.md` using the checklist template structure with these validation items:

      ```markdown
      # Specification Quality Checklist: [FEATURE NAME]

      **Purpose**: Validate specification completeness and quality before proceeding to planning
      **Created**: [DATE]
      **Feature**: [Link to spec.md]

      ## Content Quality

      - [ ] No implementation details (languages, frameworks, APIs)
      - [ ] Focused on user value and business needs
      - [ ] Written for non-technical stakeholders
      - [ ] All mandatory sections completed

      ## Requirement Completeness

      - [ ] No [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers remain
      - [ ] Requirements are testable and unambiguous
      - [ ] Success criteria are measurable
      - [ ] Success criteria are technology-agnostic (no implementation details)
      - [ ] All acceptance scenarios are defined
      - [ ] Edge cases are identified
      - [ ] Scope is clearly bounded
      - [ ] Dependencies and assumptions identified

      ## Feature Readiness

      - [ ] All functional requirements have clear acceptance criteria
      - [ ] User scenarios cover primary flows
      - [ ] Feature meets measurable outcomes defined in Success Criteria
      - [ ] No implementation details leak into specification

      ## Notes

      - Items marked incomplete require spec updates before `/speckit.clarify` or `/speckit.plan`
      ```

   b. **Run Validation Check**: Review the spec against each checklist item:
      - For each item, determine if it passes or fails
      - Document specific issues found (quote relevant spec sections)

   c. **Handle Validation Results**:

      - **If all items pass**: Mark checklist complete and proceed to the Mandatory Post-Execution Hooks section

      - **If items fail (excluding [NEEDS CLARIFICATION])**:
        1. List the failing items and specific issues
        2. Update the spec to address each issue
        3. Re-run validation until all items pass (max 3 iterations)
        4. If still failing after 3 iterations, document remaining issues in checklist notes and warn user

      - **If [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers remain**:
        1. Extract all [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: ...] markers from the spec
        2. **LIMIT CHECK**: If more than 3 markers exist, keep only the 3 most critical (by scope/security/UX impact) and make informed guesses for the rest
        3. For each clarification needed (max 3), present options to user in this format:

           ```markdown
           ## Question [N]: [Topic]

           **Context**: [Quote relevant spec section]

           **What we need to know**: [Specific question from NEEDS CLARIFICATION marker]

           **Suggested Answers**:

           | Option | Answer | Implications |
           |--------|--------|--------------|
           | A      | [First suggested answer] | [What this means for the feature] |
           | B      | [Second suggested answer] | [What this means for the feature] |
           | C      | [Third suggested answer] | [What this means for the feature] |
           | Custom | Provide your own answer | [Explain how to provide custom input] |

           **Your choice**: _[Wait for user response]_
           ```

        4. **CRITICAL - Table Formatting**: Ensure markdown tables are properly formatted:
           - Use consistent spacing with pipes aligned
           - Each cell should have spaces around content: `| Content |` not `|Content|`
           - Header separator must have at least 3 dashes: `|--------|`
           - Test that the table renders correctly in markdown preview
        5. Number questions sequentially (Q1, Q2, Q3 - max 3 total)
        6. Present all questions together before waiting for responses

290: - Date-time format: `dd/MM/yyyy, H:mm - H:mm` (24h, timezone `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`). If the activity spans multiple days: `dd/MM/yyyy H:mm - dd/MM/yyyy H:mm`. Implement in `libs/format.ts` (`formatActivityTime(start, end)`).
291: - Image fallback: if `imageUrl` is null or fails to load, show `public/images/landing/activity-placeholder.png` (HCMUS logo on faded building ΓÇö same as the placeholder thumbnails in the PNG). Remote hosts must be allowed in `next.config` (`images.remotePatterns`).
292: 
293: **Data contract**
294: 
295: ```ts
296: // features/activities/types/activity.dto.ts  (wire format ΓÇô adjust to backend)
297: export type ActivityDTO = {
298:   id: string;
299:   title: string;
300:   image_url: string | null;
301:   categories: string[];                 // e.g. ["Academic","Science"]

305:   registration_status: "open" | "upcoming" | "closed";
