216: ## 7. Section Specifications
217: 
218: ### 7.0 Site Header (global)
219: 
220: **UI**
221: - Floating white pill, horizontally centered, Γëê `24px` from top, width Γëê container width, height Γëê `56px`, soft shadow, `position: fixed/sticky`, `z-index` above hero.
222: - Left: `Logo` ΓÇö "my" in gold serif/italic + "HCMUS" in bold primary blue. Links to `/`.
223: - Center: nav links `Home ┬╖ About Us ┬╖ Activities ┬╖ Services ┬╖ Help` (14px, text color, hover ΓåÆ primary, active ΓåÆ primary + semibold or underline).
224: - Right: **Log In** button ΓÇö `Button variant="primary" size="sm"`, pill, blue, white text.
225: - Mobile: logo + hamburger (`MenuIcon`) ΓåÆ slide-down/drawer panel with the same links + auth button.
226: 
227: **Behavior**
228: - Nav items are driven by `features/landing/config/nav.ts` (`{ label, href: "#about" }`). Clicking scrolls smoothly to the anchor (`scrollToSection`) and updates the URL hash; keyboard accessible.
229: - **Scroll-spy** (`useScrollSpy(ids)` with `IntersectionObserver`) highlights the link of the section in view.
230: - On scroll > ~16px the pill may gain stronger shadow/solid background (optional polish).
231: - Auth-dependent right-side control (`useAuth()` ΓåÆ `{ user, isAuthenticated, isLoading }`):
232:   - `isLoading` ΓåÆ render a fixed-width skeleton in place of the button (no layout shift).
233:   - Guest ΓåÆ **Log In** ΓåÆ `/login`.
234:   - Authenticated ΓåÆ **Dashboard** button ΓåÆ `getDashboardPath(user.role)` (+ optional avatar/menu with Logout; reuse existing logout from `useAuth`).
235: 
236: ### 7.1 Hero (`#home`)
237: 
238: **UI**
239: - Full-width section, min-height Γëê `540ΓÇô600px` (design Γëê `540px` visible before highlights card overlaps).
240: - Background: campus building photo (`next/image`, `fill`, `priority`, `object-fit: cover`) with a **white gradient overlay** fading the photo into the page background on the left and bottom (gradient from `rgba(255,255,255,.9)` at left/bottom to transparent at right/top). Mist-like soft edge at the bottom.
241: - Content block left-aligned, top offset Γëê `140px` from page top, max-width Γëê `560px`:
242:   - **Headline** (Γëê `48px`, extra bold): "Discover. Participate. Grown." ΓÇö gold text with subtle dark text-shadow for contrast over the photo. [TBD] "Grown." is probably meant to be "Grow."; keep the copy in a constant so it is a one-line change.
243:   - **Subtitle** (Γëê `18px`, regular, dark text): "A platform for the extracurricular activities and student training scores." (wraps in 2 lines).
244:   - **CTA row** (gap Γëê `12px`):
245:     - `Get Started` ΓÇö `Button variant="white" size="lg"`, pill, primary-blue bold text, soft shadow.
246:     - `Explore the activities` ΓÇö `Button variant="primary" size="lg"`, pill. (Design typo "activites" ΓåÆ use **"activities"**.)
247: 
248: **Behavior / flow**
249: - `Get Started`: guest ΓåÆ `/login`; authenticated ΓåÆ their dashboard.
250: - `Explore the activities`: smooth-scroll to `#activities` (switch to `/activities` once that page exists ΓÇö keep the target in config).
251: - Hero image failure must not break layout (background color fallback `--color-primary-dark` at low opacity).
252: 
253: ### 7.2 Platform Highlights (`#about`)
254: 
255: **UI**
256: - A big white rounded card (`radius Γëê 28ΓÇô32px`, `--shadow-card`) horizontally inset Γëê `24px` from viewport edges, **overlapping the bottom of the hero** (negative top margin Γëê `-90px`, so hero fade passes behind it). Inner padding Γëê `48ΓÇô56px`.
257: - Header row uses `SectionHeader align="split"`:
258:   - Left: eyebrow `PLATFORM HIGHLIGHTS` (primary blue, uppercase, 14px) + title **"Built to make campus life easier"** (Γëê `32px`, bold, 2 lines).
259:   - Right (max-width Γëê `340px`, muted, 12ΓÇô13px, aligned to the right half): "Bring activities, participation, training scores, and essential campus services together in one place, making student life easier to manage and stay connected."
260: - Below: **3-column grid** of `FeatureCard` (gap Γëê `40px`). Each card:
261:   - Image (Γëê `16:9`-ish, Γëê `205├ù105` in design, small radius `4ΓÇô8px`, `object-fit: cover`).
262:   - Title (Γëê `16px`, semibold).
263:   - Description (Γëê `12ΓÇô13px`, muted, 3 lines).
264: - Items (from `config/highlights.ts`):

284: - The second featured card in the PNG is a **design placeholder** showing labels "Key Tags / TIME / Location / Registration Status: Open/Closed/Upcoming" ΓÇö it documents the *possible values*, not a different layout. Render it identically to the first featured card with real data.
285: - Status badge mapping (`registrationStatus`):
286:   - `open` ΓåÆ success (green dot) "Registration Open"
287:   - `upcoming` ΓåÆ warning/info dot "Registration Upcoming" (registration not yet started)

293: **Data contract**

333: function useLandingActivities(): {

337: // Cancels the request on unmount (AbortController). One automatic retry is optional; manual retry via refetch().

340: **State machine ΓåÆ UI** (`ActivitiesSection` renders the header always, then one body):
341: 
342: | Status | Body |
343: |--------|------|
344: | `loading` | `ActivitiesSkeleton`: same grid footprint ΓÇö 2 featured skeleton cards + 3 compact skeleton rows (image block, 3 text lines, footer line). `aria-busy="true"`. Prevents layout shift. |

Please check back soon."** Optional action: none for guests; do not render the grid frame. (Same height Γëê one card row to avoid a collapsing section.) |

349: **Layout rules (`ActivityGrid`)**

351: 2. `featured.length ΓëÑ 1`, `upcoming.length === 0` ΓåÆ featured cards only, equal-width columns spanning the container (no empty right column).
352: 3. `featured.length === 0`, `upcoming.length ΓëÑ 1` ΓåÆ render upcoming items with the **featured card variant** in a responsive grid (max 3 columns).
353: 4. Both empty ΓåÆ `empty` state (never render an empty grid).
354: - Mobile: single column; compact cards keep horizontal layout.
355: 
356: ### 7.4 HCMUS Services ΓÇö Quick Access (`#services`) ΓÇö auth-gated
357: 
358: **UI**
359: - Full-bleed section, background `--color-primary-dark`, padding Γëê `64px` vertical. White text on top (`SectionHeader tone="dark"`): eyebrow `HCMUS SERVICES` (uppercase, small, white/70%) + title **"Quick access to essential university services"** (Γëê `32px` bold, left aligned, 2 lines).
360: - Grid of `ServiceCard`: **3 columns ├ù 2 rows** (gap Γëê `32px` column, `24px` row), each card:
361:   - White pill/rounded container (Γëê `240├ù64`, radius Γëê `32px`), left: service icon/logo tile (Γëê `48px`, rounded), then service name (bold Γëê `16ΓÇô18px`, dark) and below it a small blue link text **"Access ΓåÆ"** (`ArrowRightIcon`).
362: - Services (from `config/services.ts`; order = row-major):
363:   1. Moodle (fit@hcmus logo) ΓÇö public
364:   2. Tuition Payment ΓÇö locked for guests
365:   3. [TBD name, light-blue icon] ΓÇö locked
366:   4. Student Portal (blue icon) ΓÇö public
367:   5. HCMUS Website (green icon) ΓÇö locked
368:   6. [TBD name, red icon] ΓÇö locked
369: 
370: ```ts
371: type ServiceItem = {
372:   id: string; name: string; href: string;        // external URL
373:   icon: { src: string; alt: string };
374:   access: "public" | "authenticated";            // authenticated => blurred for guests
375: };

377: 
378: **Guest vs authenticated behavior (key requirement)**
379: - **Guest** (`!isAuthenticated`): items with `access: "public"` (first column in the design: Moodle, Student Portal) render normally and are clickable. Items with `access: "authenticated"` render **blurred** ("half visible, half hidden"):
380:   - CSS `filter: blur(6pxΓÇô8px)` (blur grows slightly toward the right edge in the design: column 2 Γëê light, column 3 Γëê heavier ΓÇö implement with per-column blur or a left-to-right mask; a single uniform blur is acceptable), reduced opacity Γëê `0.85`.

384: - `isLoading`: render the **guest (locked) version** to avoid showing protected cards for a flash; unlock when resolved. DOM structure is identical so there is no layout shift.

386: - External links: `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Card hover: slight lift/shadow; focus-visible ring (white on blue).

388: ### 7.5 Help / Guide (`#help`)
389: 
390: **UI**

400: | Title | Subtitle | Target |
401: |-------|----------|--------|
402: | GETTING STARTED | Learn the basics | `/help#getting-started` |
403: | ACTIVITIES | How to register? | `/help#activities` |

406: 
407:   [ASSUMPTION] `/help` does not exist yet; keep hrefs in config so they can be repointed. Until the page exists, links may be disabled (`aria-disabled`) or point to a "coming soon" page ΓÇö decide with the team.
408: 
409: **Behavior**: whole card is a link; hover ΓåÆ arrow nudges right Γëê `4px`, shadow increases; keyboard focus ring.
410: 
411: ### 7.6 Footer (`#contact`)
412: 
413: **UI**
414: - Full-bleed `--color-primary-dark`, large vertical padding (design shows a tall block Γëê `260px`), white text.
415: - Design is a **placeholder**: heading "Footer" and "Contact services, HotlinesΓÇª." **[TBD]** final content. Implement the component structure now so content can be dropped in via `config/footer.ts`:
416:   - Brand column: `Logo` (light variant) + one-line description.
417:   - Contact column: address, hotline(s), email.
418:   - Quick links column: Home, About Us, Activities, Services, Help (reuse `nav.ts`).
419:   - Bottom bar: copyright `┬⌐ {year} HCMUS` (year computed, not hardcoded).
420: - Phone/email render as `tel:` / `mailto:` links.
421: - Component: `components/layout/SiteFooter.tsx`, reusable on other public pages.
422: 
423: ---
424: 
425: ## 8. User Flows
426: 
427: ### 8.1 Guest ΓÇö first visit
428: 1. Lands on `/` ΓåÆ header (Log In), hero, highlights render immediately (static).
429: 2. `ActivitiesSection` mounts ΓåÆ skeleton ΓåÆ API ΓåÆ (success | empty | error) per ┬º7.3.
430: 3. Scrolls to Services: sees Moodle + Student Portal clearly, other cards blurred + (optional) "Log in to see all services".
431: 4. Clicks **Log In** (header / overlay / Get Started) ΓåÆ `/login` (return target preserved). After login, `AuthProvider` sets the user and the app redirects to the role dashboard (existing auth flow) or back to `#services` if `redirectTo` is used.
432: 5. Clicks an activity card ΓåÆ `/activities/{id}` [ASSUMPTION: detail page is publicly viewable; registering requires login].

435: ### 8.2 Authenticated user (student / organizer / admin)

442: - Slow response: skeleton persists (no timeout UI needed; abort on unmount).
443: - 2xx with data: render per layout rules.
444: - 2xx with empty lists: empty state (not an error).
445: - Network/5xx/invalid payload: error state + **Try again** (re-enters `loading`).
446: - 401/403 must not occur (public endpoint); if it does, treat as `error`.

453: ## 9. Non-functional Requirements

455: - **Accessibility**: semantic landmarks (`header`, `main`, `section[aria-labelledby]`, `footer`); one `h1` (hero headline), section titles `h2`, card titles `h3`; visible focus rings; meaningful `alt` for content images, `alt=""` for decoration; contrast ΓëÑ 4.5:1 (check gold headline over photo ΓÇö keep text-shadow); respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (disable smooth scroll/lift animations); blurred locked cards hidden from assistive tech.

463: 
464: ## 10. Implementation Order (suggested)

466: 1. Design tokens in `globals.css`; `components/ui/*` primitives and icons.
467: 2. `SiteHeader`, `SiteFooter`, `Logo`; move landing route to `app/(public)/page.tsx`.

# myHCMUS ΓÇö Landing Page Specification

> Audience: a coding agent (and human reviewers) implementing the public landing page at route `/`.
> Source of truth for visuals: the Figma/PNG desktop design (`docs/ui/landing-page-ui.png`). Values marked **(approx.)** were estimated from the PNG and must be verified against Figma.

---

## 1. Purpose & Scope

The landing page is the public entry point of **myHCMUS**, a platform for extracurricular activities and student training scores (DRS) at HCMUS.

Goals:
1. Explain what the platform does (hero + highlights).
2. Showcase featured/upcoming activities, fetched from an API, with complete loading / empty / error handling.
3. Give quick access to university services; **guests see only part of them**, the rest is blurred to motivate login.
4. Point to help content and provide contact info (footer).

Out of scope: login form (`/login`), dashboards, the activity detail page, the full activities list page, About Us and Help pages. Only their **links** are wired from here.

## 1. Purpose & Scope

The landing page is the public entry point of **myHCMUS**, a platform for extracurricular activities and student training scores (DRS) at HCMUS.

Goals:
1. Explain what the platform does (hero + highlights).
2. Showcase featured/upcoming activities, fetched from an API, with complete loading / empty / error handling.
3. Give quick access to university services; **guests see only part of them**, the rest is blurred to motivate login.
4. Point to help content and provide contact info (footer).

Out of scope: login form (`/login`), dashboards, the activity detail page, the full activities list page, About Us and Help pages. Only their **links** are wired from here.

---

## 2. Page Anatomy

A global header floats over the hero. The page body has **6 sections**:

| # | Section | Anchor id | Background | Data source |
|---|---------|-----------|------------|-------------|
| 0 | Site Header (global, floating) | ΓÇö | white pill over hero | static nav config + auth state |
| 1 | Hero | `home` | campus photo + white gradient | static |
| 2 | Platform Highlights | `about` | white card overlapping hero | static config |
| 3 | Featured & Upcoming Activities | `activities` | page background (white/very light) | **API** |
| 4 | HCMUS Services (Quick Access) | `services` | full-bleed deep blue | static config + **auth state** |
| 5 | Help / Guide | `help` | white with decorative blue circles | static config |
| 6 | Footer | `contact` | full-bleed deep blue | static config |

Header nav items map to anchors: Home ΓåÆ `#home`, About Us ΓåÆ `#about`, Activities ΓåÆ `#activities`, Services ΓåÆ `#services`, Help ΓåÆ `#help`.

---

## 3. Fit with the Existing Frontend

Existing structure (Next.js App Router): `app/(public)`, `app/(protected)/{admin,organizer,student}`, `features/auth/*` (context, provider, schema, services + mock service, types, DTO), `hooks/useAuth.ts`, `libs/{api-client,navigation,roles,session}.ts`, `components/{forms,icons}`, `types/{api,entities}.ts`.

Follow the same conventions already used by `features/auth`:
- Feature-first folders under `features/<name>/`.
- **Service + mock service** pair behind one interface (see `auth.service.ts` / `mock.auth.service.ts`). Reuse whatever switching mechanism auth uses (env flag or factory) ΓÇö do not invent a second one.
- **DTO vs domain type separation** (`*.dto.ts` = wire format, `*.ts` = UI model) with a mapper.
- One icon per file in `components/icons`.
- HTTP goes through `libs/api-client.ts` only; no raw `fetch` in components.
- Role ΓåÆ dashboard resolution uses `libs/roles.ts` / `libs/navigation.ts`. If a `getDashboardPath(role)` helper does not exist yet, add it there (do not hardcode paths in components).

### 3.1 Routing

- Landing route: **`app/(public)/page.tsx`** ΓåÆ renders `<LandingPage />` from `features/landing`.
- **Remove or empty the current `app/page.tsx`** ΓÇö two files resolving to `/` conflict.
- `app/(public)/layout.tsx` currently serves `/login`; check what it renders. The landing page composes `SiteHeader` / `SiteFooter` itself (inside `LandingPage`) so `/login` is not affected. If more marketing pages appear later, extract a `(site)` route group with a shared layout.
- The landing page is **always accessible**, including for authenticated users (no auto-redirect to dashboard). Authenticated users get a "Dashboard" button in the header and unlocked services.

### 3.2 Rendering strategy

- `app/(public)/page.tsx` is a **Server Component** (static shell, SEO metadata).
- Interactive/stateful parts are Client Components (`"use client"`): `SiteHeader` (auth state, mobile menu, scroll-spy), `ActivitiesSection` (data fetch states), `ServicesSection` (auth gating).
- Activities are fetched **client-side** through a hook so a slow/failed API never blocks the page. [ASSUMPTION] If the project already uses React Query/SWR in `providers/provider.tsx`, use it inside the hook instead of hand-rolled state; the hook's return contract stays the same.

---

## 5. Design Tokens (approx.)

## 6. Shared Reusable Components (contracts)

244: ## Data Flow
245: 
246: ### Page and navigation
247: 
248: ```text
249: Request /
250: ΓåÆ (public)/page.tsx (server metadata + shell)
251: ΓåÆ LandingPage (server composition)
252: ΓåÆ SiteHeader (client)
253:    Γö£ΓöÇ useAuth() ΓåÆ Log In | Dashboard | reserved skeleton
254:    Γö£ΓöÇ useScrollSpy(sectionIds) ΓåÆ aria-current and visible active cue
255:    ΓööΓöÇ mobile dialog ΓåÆ same links + auth action
256: ΓåÆ Section anchors update history and scroll below the floating header
257: ```
258: 
259: - Section links use `scrollToSection(id)`, which updates the URL hash with `history.pushState`, scrolls the section into view with an offset, and respects reduced motion.
260: - Direct hashes and browser back/forward restore the target section through `hashchange`/`popstate` handling.
261: - The header login link carries the active section as a same-origin return path: `getLoginHref("/#services")`.
262: 
263: ### Authentication and return behavior
264: 
265: ```text
266: Guest header "Log In"
267: ΓåÆ /login?redirectTo=<encoded landing location>
268: ΓåÆ (public)/login/page.tsx reads searchParams.redirectTo and passes it to LoginForm
269: ΓåÆ LoginForm sanitizes and uses the value
270: ΓåÆ successful auth
271: ΓåÆ router.replace(safeRedirectTo ?? getDashboardPath(user.role))
272: 
273: Guest hero "Get Started"
274: ΓåÆ /login (no landing return target)
275: ΓåÆ successful auth
276: ΓåÆ role dashboard
277: 
278: Signed-in hero/header action
279: ΓåÆ getDashboardPath(user.role)
280: ```
281: 
282: - `getDashboardPath(role)` resolves the Dashboard entry from `NAVIGATION_ITEMS` so paths are not hardcoded in components.
283: - `redirectTo` is accepted only when it is a same-origin absolute path beginning with `/`, not `//`, contains no backslashes or control characters, resolves to the current origin, and does not target `/login`. Invalid values fall back to the role dashboard.
284: - The login route is an async Server Component that reads the Next.js `searchParams` promise and passes `redirectTo` to `LoginForm` as a prop. This avoids a client `useSearchParams` dependency and keeps the existing scratch page that renders `LoginForm` without a Suspense boundary working.
285: 
286: ### Activity discovery
287: 
288: ```text
289: ActivitiesSection (client)
290: ΓåÆ useLandingActivities()
291: ΓåÆ createActivityService()
292:    Γö£ΓöÇ MockActivityService ΓåÆ deterministic DTO fixtures ΓåÆ activity.mapper ΓåÆ domain
293:    ΓööΓöÇ RealActivityService ΓåÆ api.get("/activities/landing", { signal })
294:         ΓåÆ provisional response DTO ΓåÆ activity.mapper ΓåÆ domain
295: ΓåÆ discriminated state
296:    Γö£ΓöÇ loading ΓåÆ ActivitiesSkeleton (2 featured + 3 compact footprints)
297:    Γö£ΓöÇ success ΓåÆ ActivityGrid ΓåÆ ActivityCard
298:    Γö£ΓöÇ empty ΓåÆ EmptyState
299:    ΓööΓöÇ error ΓåÆ ErrorState with Try again ΓåÆ refetch
300: ```
301: 
302: - The hook aborts in-flight requests on unmount and before a retry; a late response cannot overwrite a newer outcome.
303: - The mapper filters unusable items first, then applies display caps: grouped mode keeps up to two featured and three compact items; single-list mode keeps up to five items and renders them in the featured style.
304: - The mapper throws a typed mapping error when the payload cannot be interpreted or when raw items were supplied but none are usable. The hook turns that into the error state.
305: - The rest of the page is server-rendered and remains usable regardless of the activity outcome.
306: - Activity service/mapping failures are contained by the hook's error state. No class-based section error boundary is added because class components are prohibited; if a render-time boundary becomes necessary, use the App Router's `error.tsx` pattern or a compliant future primitive.
307: 
308: ### Services gating
309: 
310: ```text
311: ServicesSection (client)
312: ΓåÆ useAuth() ΓåÆ isLoading | guest | authenticated
313: ΓåÆ config/services.ts
314:    Γö£ΓöÇ isLoading or guest ΓåÆ public cards usable; authenticated-only cards locked
315:    ΓööΓöÇ authenticated ΓåÆ all cards usable
316: ```
317: 
318: - Locked cards are not links, expose no destination, are inert, have `aria-hidden="true"`, and are excluded from keyboard navigation.
319: - The locked and unlocked states use the same outer dimensions so unlocking does not shift layout.
320: - No separate invitation overlay is rendered over locked cards; the header Log In action is the sign-in path.

322: ## API Integration Strategy
323: 
324: ### Provisional HTTP contract
325: 
326: The backend contract is **not confirmed**. The plan uses one isolated provisional shape so a contract change affects only the DTO, mapper, and real service:
327: 
328: ```text
329: GET /activities/landing
330: Auth: public
331: Response 200: { data: GroupedLandingActivitiesDTO | ListLandingActivitiesDTO }
332: Response 5xx/network/invalid payload: error outcome
333: ```
334: 
335: - `GroupedLandingActivitiesDTO` contains `featured` and `upcoming` arrays.
336: - `ListLandingActivitiesDTO` contains a single `activities` array.
337: - The existing `types/api.ts` `ActionResult<T>` is not reused as a GET envelope because it models an application result, not an HTTP response. The provisional `{ data: ... }` envelope is documented as an assumption and cannot leak into components.
338: - If the confirmed backend contract differs, only `activity.dto.ts`, the mapper, and `RealActivityService` change; the service interface, hook, and UI remain stable.
339: 
340: ### API client extension
341: 
342: - Extend `api.get` to accept optional `RequestInit` options so the activity service can pass an `AbortSignal`:
343: 
344: ```ts
345: get: <T>(endpoint: string, options?: Omit<RequestOptions, "body" | "method">) =>
346:   apiRequest<T>(endpoint, "GET", options)
347: ```
348: 
349: - Keep base URL resolution, headers, serialization, and error normalization in `src/libs/api-client.ts`.
350: - Replace touched `any` signatures with `unknown` where safe; do not introduce new `any` in production code.
351: - Use the existing normalized `Error`; the UI shows fixed user-facing copy and never renders a raw server error.
352: 
353: ### Real service
354: 
355: - `RealActivityService implements ActivityService`.
356: - It calls `api.get<LandingActivitiesResponseDTO>("/activities/landing", { signal })`.
357: - It passes `response.data` to `mapLandingActivitiesDTO`.
358: - It does not construct URLs or handle authentication headers itself.
359: 
360: ### Selection and mock strategy
361: 
362: - `src/libs/service-mode.ts` exposes one selection helper based on `NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE`; the default is `mock` until the backend contract is confirmed.
363: - `activity.service.factory.ts` is the only production module that imports both implementations.
364: - `NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE=api` selects the real service; any other value selects the mock.
365: - `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_ACTIVITY_SCENARIO` controls deterministic mock fixtures: `success`, `partial`, `empty`, `error`, `delay`, `single-list`, and malformed-for-error cases.
366: - Tests inject a mock service instance or a deferred fake directly into the hook, avoiding environment dependence.
367: 
368: ### Images
369: 
370: - Use local landing assets initially; do not add a remote host until the media host is confirmed.
371: - Hero image uses `next/image` with `preload` (Next.js 16; `priority` is deprecated) and `sizes="100vw"`.
372: - Below-the-fold images are lazy by default and reserve aspect-ratio dimensions.
373: - Activity images use a shared `ActivityImage` wrapper with an `onError` fallback to `activity-placeholder.png`; dimensions remain stable.
374: - Real activity image hosts require a confirmed `images.remotePatterns` allowlist. This is a release dependency, not an assumption to guess.

376: ## State Management
377: 
378: ### Activity state machine
379: 
380: ```text
381: idle ΓåÆ loading ΓåÆ success | empty | error
382:                  Γåæ                Γöé
383:                  ΓööΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇ refetch ΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇΓöÿ
384: ```
385: 
386: | State | Data | UI |
387: |-------|------|----|
388: | `loading` | `null` | Grouped skeleton footprint; region is `aria-busy="true"`; header remains visible |
389: | `success` | `LandingActivities` | Layout rules in `ActivityGrid`; cards use domain data |
390: | `empty` | zero usable items | EmptyState with the specified message and reserved height |
391: | `error` | `null` | ErrorState with Try again; no raw error text |
392: 
393: Implementation details:
394: 
395: - `useReducer` or an equivalent discriminated union keeps transitions explicit and prevents impossible combinations.
396: - `refetch()` aborts the current request, returns to `loading`, and starts a new request.
397: - The hook ignores aborted requests and responses from older request IDs.
398: - The hook never throws into render; it converts service and mapping failures into the error state.
399: - No global state library or data-fetching library is added. A single-section fetch does not justify a runtime dependency.
400: 
401: ### Other local state
402: 
403: - **Header auth action**: `useAuth()` supplies `isLoading`, `isAuthenticated`, and `user`; a fixed-width placeholder prevents layout shift and prevents a signed-in-only action from flashing.
404: - **Services**: `isLoading` is treated as locked; the same DOM structure unlocks without layout shift.
405: - **Mobile drawer**: local open state backed by a native modal `<dialog>`; native focus containment, Escape handling, backdrop styling, body scroll lock, and focus restoration.
406: - **Scroll-spy**: `useScrollSpy` uses `IntersectionObserver` with a header-aware root margin; active state is exposed with `aria-current="location"` plus a visible non-color cue.
407: - **Hero actions**: while auth resolves, Get Started uses the guest-safe login path; the proxy redirects an existing session from `/login` to the dashboard if applicable.
408: - **Static content**: navigation, hero copy, shared section headers, highlights, services, guides, footer, and SEO values live in `features/landing/config/*.ts`; activity section header, status labels, and empty/error messages live in `features/activities/config.ts`. No copy is duplicated in components.
409: 
410: ## Responsive and Accessibility Design
411: 
412: - Use Tailwind's default `sm` (640px) and `lg` (1024px) breakpoints; no custom breakpoint set is needed.
413: - At `lg` and above: three highlight columns, 3x2 services, 2x2 guides, and the two-featured-plus-three-compact activity layout.
414: - At `sm` to `lg - 1`: header uses the modal drawer, highlights/services use two columns, guides keep two columns, featured activities use two columns, and compact activities form a two-column stack below.
415: - Below `sm`: one column for highlights, services, and guides; hero actions stack full width; compact activity cards keep their horizontal presentation.
416: - Header height and `scroll-margin-top` share a token so anchors land below the floating header.
417: - The page uses `header`, `main`, `section`, and `footer` landmarks; one `h1`; section titles are `h2`; card titles are `h3`.
418: - Activity titles are rendered exactly as supplied. Do not apply `text-transform: uppercase` to activity content, even though the mock may supply uppercase strings.
419: - Status badges combine text, an icon/dot, and color; color is never the only cue.
420: - The mobile drawer uses semantic `<dialog>` and a labeled close control; background content is inert while open; focus returns to the trigger when it closes without navigation.
421: - Loading, empty, and error outcomes are announced through a polite status region without moving focus unexpectedly. On retry, focus moves to the stable activity section heading/container rather than being dropped to the page start; the terminal outcome is announced without further focus movement.
422: - Focus-visible rings use a shared token; no focus outline is removed without a replacement.
423: - Reduced motion disables smooth scrolling, hover lift, and pulse animation while preserving visible state changes.
424: - Touch targets are at least 44x44px; interactive text and indicators meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast.

**Structure Decision**: The repository is a single Next.js web application. The feature uses the existing App Router route groups, feature-first layout, shared `libs`, shared UI/layout component layers, and the existing auth hook. The only structural move is replacing the conflicting root page with the route-group page required by the source design.

## Data Flow

### Page and navigation

```text
Request /
ΓåÆ (public)/page.tsx (server metadata + shell)
ΓåÆ LandingPage (server composition)
ΓåÆ SiteHeader (client)
   Γö£ΓöÇ useAuth() ΓåÆ Log In | Dashboard | reserved skeleton
   Γö£ΓöÇ useScrollSpy(sectionIds) ΓåÆ aria-current and visible active cue
   ΓööΓöÇ mobile dialog ΓåÆ same links + auth action
ΓåÆ Section anchors update history and scroll below the floating header
```

- Section links use `scrollToSection(id)`, which updates the URL hash with `history.pushState`, scrolls the section into view with an offset, and respects reduced motion.
- Direct hashes and browser back/forward restore the target section through `hashchange`/`popstate` handling.
- The header login link carries the active section as a same-origin return path: `getLoginHref("/#services")`.

### Authentication and return behavior

```text
Guest header "Log In"
ΓåÆ /login?redirectTo=<encoded landing location>
ΓåÆ (public)/login/page.tsx reads searchParams.redirectTo and passes it to LoginForm
ΓåÆ LoginForm sanitizes and uses the value
ΓåÆ successful auth
ΓåÆ router.replace(safeRedirectTo ?? getDashboardPath(user.role))

Guest hero "Get Started"
ΓåÆ /login (no landing return target)
ΓåÆ successful auth
ΓåÆ role dashboard

Signed-in hero/header action
ΓåÆ getDashboardPath(user.role)
```

- `getDashboardPath(role)` resolves the Dashboard entry from `NAVIGATION_ITEMS` so paths are not hardcoded in components.
- `redirectTo` is accepted only when it is a same-origin absolute path beginning with `/`, not `//`, contains no backslashes or control characters, resolves to the current origin, and does not target `/login`. Invalid values fall back to the role dashboard.
- The login route is an async Server Component that reads the Next.js `searchParams` promise and passes `redirectTo` to `LoginForm` as a prop. This avoids a client `useSearchParams` dependency and keeps the existing scratch page that renders `LoginForm` without a Suspense boundary working.

### Activity discovery

```text
ActivitiesSection (client)
ΓåÆ useLandingActivities()
ΓåÆ createActivityService()
   Γö£ΓöÇ MockActivityService ΓåÆ deterministic DTO fixtures ΓåÆ activity.mapper ΓåÆ domain
   ΓööΓöÇ RealActivityService ΓåÆ api.get("/activities/landing", { signal })
        ΓåÆ provisional response DTO ΓåÆ activity.mapper ΓåÆ domain
ΓåÆ discriminated state
   Γö£ΓöÇ loading ΓåÆ ActivitiesSkeleton (2 featured + 3 compact footprints)
   Γö£ΓöÇ success ΓåÆ ActivityGrid ΓåÆ ActivityCard
   Γö£ΓöÇ empty ΓåÆ EmptyState
   ΓööΓöÇ error ΓåÆ ErrorState with Try again ΓåÆ refetch
```

- The hook aborts in-flight requests on unmount and before a retry; a late response cannot overwrite a newer outcome.
- The mapper filters unusable items first, then applies display caps: grouped mode keeps up to two featured and three compact items; single-list mode keeps up to five items and renders them in the featured style.
- The mapper throws a typed mapping error when the payload cannot be interpreted or when raw items were supplied but none are usable. The hook turns that into the error state.
- The rest of the page is server-rendered and remains usable regardless of the activity outcome.
- Activity service/mapping failures are contained by the hook's error state. No class-based section error boundary is added because class components are prohibited; if a render-time boundary becomes necessary, use the App Router's `error.tsx` pattern or a compliant future primitive.

### Services gating

```text
ServicesSection (client)
ΓåÆ useAuth() ΓåÆ isLoading | guest | authenticated
ΓåÆ config/services.ts
   Γö£ΓöÇ isLoading or guest ΓåÆ public cards usable; authenticated-only cards locked
   ΓööΓöÇ authenticated ΓåÆ all cards usable
```

- Locked cards are not links, expose no destination, are inert, have `aria-hidden="true"`, and are excluded from keyboard navigation.
- The locked and unlocked states use the same outer dimensions so unlocking does not shift layout.
- No separate invitation overlay is rendered over locked cards; the header Log In action is the sign-in path.

## API Integration Strategy

### Provisional HTTP contract

The backend contract is **not confirmed**. The plan uses one isolated provisional shape so a contract change affects only the DTO, mapper, and real service:

```text
GET /activities/landing
Auth: public
Response 200: { data: GroupedLandingActivitiesDTO | ListLandingActivitiesDTO }
Response 5xx/network/invalid payload: error outcome
```

- `GroupedLandingActivitiesDTO` contains `featured` and `upcoming` arrays.
- `ListLandingActivitiesDTO` contains a single `activities` array.
- The existing `types/api.ts` `ActionResult<T>` is not reused as a GET envelope because it models an application result, not an HTTP response. The provisional `{ data: ... }` envelope is documented as an assumption and cannot leak into components.
- If the confirmed backend contract differs, only `activity.dto.ts`, the mapper, and `RealActivityService` change; the service interface, hook, and UI remain stable.

### API client extension

- Extend `api.get` to accept optional `RequestInit` options so the activity service can pass an `AbortSignal`:

```ts
get: <T>(endpoint: string, options?: Omit<RequestOptions, "body" | "method">) =>
  apiRequest<T>(endpoint, "GET", options)
```

- Keep base URL resolution, headers, serialization, and error normalization in `src/libs/api-client.ts`.
- Replace touched `any` signatures with `unknown` where safe; do not introduce new `any` in production code.
- Use the existing normalized `Error`; the UI shows fixed user-facing copy and never renders a raw server error.

### Real service

- `RealActivityService implements ActivityService`.
- It calls `api.get<LandingActivitiesResponseDTO>("/activities/landing", { signal })`.
- It passes `response.data` to `mapLandingActivitiesDTO`.
- It does not construct URLs or handle authentication headers itself.

### Selection and mock strategy

- `src/libs/service-mode.ts` exposes one selection helper based on `NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE`; the default is `mock` until the backend contract is confirmed.
- `activity.service.factory.ts` is the only production module that imports both implementations.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE=api` selects the real service; any other value selects the mock.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_ACTIVITY_SCENARIO` controls deterministic mock fixtures: `success`, `partial`, `empty`, `error`, `delay`, `single-list`, and malformed-for-error cases.
- Tests inject a mock service instance or a deferred fake directly into the hook, avoiding environment dependence.

### Images

- Use local landing assets initially; do not add a remote host until the media host is confirmed.
- Hero image uses `next/image` with `preload` (Next.js 16; `priority` is deprecated) and `sizes="100vw"`.
- Below-the-fold images are lazy by default and reserve aspect-ratio dimensions.
- Activity images use a shared `ActivityImage` wrapper with an `onError` fallback to `activity-placeholder.png`; dimensions remain stable.
- Real activity image hosts require a confirmed `images.remotePatterns` allowlist. This is a release dependency, not an assumption to guess.

## State Management

### Activity state machine

```text
idle ΓåÆ loading ΓåÆ success | empty | error
                 Γåæ                Γöé
                 ΓööΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇ refetch ΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇΓöÿ
```

| State | Data | UI |
|-------|------|----|
| `loading` | `null` | Grouped skeleton footprint; region is `aria-busy="true"`; header remains visible |
| `success` | `LandingActivities` | Layout rules in `ActivityGrid`; cards use domain data |
| `empty` | zero usable items | EmptyState with the specified message and reserved height |
| `error` | `null` | ErrorState with Try again; no raw error text |

Implementation details:

- `useReducer` or an equivalent discriminated union keeps transitions explicit and prevents impossible combinations.
- `refetch()` aborts the current request, returns to `loading`, and starts a new request.
- The hook ignores aborted requests and responses from older request IDs.
- The hook never throws into render; it converts service and mapping failures into the error state.
- No global state library or data-fetching library is added. A single-section fetch does not justify a runtime dependency.

### Other local state

- **Header auth action**: `useAuth()` supplies `isLoading`, `isAuthenticated`, and `user`; a fixed-width placeholder prevents layout shift and prevents a signed-in-only action from flashing.
- **Services**: `isLoading` is treated as locked; the same DOM structure unlocks without layout shift.
- **Mobile drawer**: local open state backed by a native modal `<dialog>`; native focus containment, Escape handling, backdrop styling, body scroll lock, and focus restoration.
- **Scroll-spy**: `useScrollSpy` uses `IntersectionObserver` with a header-aware root margin; active state is exposed with `aria-current="location"` plus a visible non-color cue.
- **Hero actions**: while auth resolves, Get Started uses the guest-safe login path; the proxy redirects an existing session from `/login` to the dashboard if applicable.
- **Static content**: navigation, hero copy, shared section headers, highlights, services, guides, footer, and SEO values live in `features/landing/config/*.ts`; activity section header, status labels, and empty/error messages live in `features/activities/config.ts`. No copy is duplicated in components.

## Responsive and Accessibility Design

- Use Tailwind's default `sm` (640px) and `lg` (1024px) breakpoints; no custom breakpoint set is needed.
- At `lg` and above: three highlight columns, 3x2 services, 2x2 guides, and the two-featured-plus-three-compact activity layout.
- At `sm` to `lg - 1`: header uses the modal drawer, highlights/services use two columns, guides keep two columns, featured activities use two columns, and compact activities form a two-column stack below.
- Below `sm`: one column for highlights, services, and guides; hero actions stack full width; compact activity cards keep their horizontal presentation.
- Header height and `scroll-margin-top` share a token so anchors land below the floating header.
- The page uses `header`, `main`, `section`, and `footer` landmarks; one `h1`; section titles are `h2`; card titles are `h3`.
- Activity titles are rendered exactly as supplied. Do not apply `text-transform: uppercase` to activity content, even though the mock may supply uppercase strings.
- Status badges combine text, an icon/dot, and color; color is never the only cue.
- The mobile drawer uses semantic `<dialog>` and a labeled close control; background content is inert while open; focus returns to the trigger when it closes without navigation.
- Loading, empty, and error outcomes are announced through a polite status region without moving focus unexpectedly. On retry, focus moves to the stable activity section heading/container rather than being dropped to the page start; the terminal outcome is announced without further focus movement.
- Focus-visible rings use a shared token; no focus outline is removed without a replacement.
- Reduced motion disables smooth scrolling, hover lift, and pulse animation while preserving visible state changes.
- Touch targets are at least 44x44px; interactive text and indicators meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast.

## Design Tokens and Typography

Add the following to `src/app/globals.css` through the Tailwind `@theme` layer (names may be adapted to Tailwind v4 conventions, but values remain tokenized):

| Token | Value | Use |
|-------|-------|-----|
| `--color-primary` | `#1F4FA3` | primary actions, links, eyebrow text |
| `--color-primary-dark` | `#17409A` | services/footer backgrounds |
| `--color-accent-gold` | `#F2B31B` | hero highlight and logo accent |
| `--color-text` | `#111827` | headings and body |
| `--color-text-muted` | `#6B7280` | descriptions and metadata |
| `--color-surface` | `#FFFFFF` | cards and header |
| `--color-success` | `#16A34A` | registration open |
| `--color-warning` | `#D97706` | registration upcoming |
| `--color-neutral-status` | `#6B7280` | registration closed |
| `--color-guide-gradient-from` | `#FFFFFF` | guide card top |
| `--color-guide-gradient-to` | `#E3EEFB` | guide card bottom |
| `--radius-card` | `24px` | cards |
| `--radius-pill` | `9999px` | buttons/header |
| `--shadow-card` | `0 8px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.10)` | cards |
| `--container-landing` | `1200px` | content container |
| `--page-gutter` | `24px` | horizontal page padding |
| `--header-height` | `56px` | header and scroll offset |
| `--focus-ring` | token-backed focus color/width | visible focus |

- The current `app/layout.tsx` imports Geist but never instantiates it, so `--font-geist-sans` is undefined and `globals.css` falls back to Arial. Wire the existing import with `Geist({ variable: "--font-geist-sans", subsets: ["latin"] })` and apply its variable class; do not add a new font package. Validate the visual match against the UI reference before choosing an alternative.
- Set the body font family from the token layer rather than leaving the current Arial fallback.
- The current `prefers-color-scheme: dark` override is not part of the landing design. Remove or neutralize it for the landing surface, or explicitly set the landing shell to light surface tokens. No dark theme is in scope.
- All new components use token-backed Tailwind utilities or CSS variables. No hex values in JSX or component class strings.

## Testing Strategy

### Tooling

Add development-only dependencies and scripts:

- `vitest`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `jsdom`, `vite-tsconfig-paths`
- `@testing-library/react`, `@testing-library/jest-dom`, `@testing-library/user-event`
- `axe-core` for automated accessibility checks

Add `"test": "vitest run"` and `"test:watch": "vitest"` to `package.json`. These are dev-only; no runtime dependency is introduced. The constitution's dependency justification is: there is no existing test runner, and the feature requires deterministic verification of mappers, state transitions, gating, and accessibility. `tests/setup.ts` provides the Testing Library matchers, `matchMedia`, `IntersectionObserver`, `scrollIntoView`, and `HTMLDialogElement.showModal`/`close` shims because jsdom does not implement them. Tests mock `next/image` and `next/navigation` where the real implementations require the Next.js runtime.

### Unit and component tests

- `libs/format.test.ts`:
  - same-day format, multi-day format, leading-zero hour/minutes, midnight, Vietnam timezone boundary, invalid dates.
- `libs/navigation.test.ts`:
  - `getDashboardPath` for all roles; `getLoginHref` encoding; safe redirect accepts valid landing paths and rejects absolute URLs, protocol-relative URLs, backslashes, control characters, and `/login`; invalid values fall back correctly.
- `features/activities/mappers/activity.mapper.test.ts`:
  - grouped and single-list payloads; required/optional fields; invalid items dropped; all-invalid payload throws; reversed/invalid intervals rejected; caps applied after filtering; href encoding; status mapping; title preservation.
- `features/activities/services/activity.service.test.ts`:
  - `RealActivityService` calls the API client with `/activities/landing` and the supplied signal, unwraps `data`, and maps; API errors propagate; `MockActivityService` satisfies the same interface and scenario contract.
- `features/activities/hooks/useLandingActivities.test.tsx`:
  - loading, success, empty, error; retry transitions; abort on unmount; stale response ignored; repeated retry settles once; mapper error becomes error state. Use a deferred fake service; no environment variables.
- `features/activities/components/ActivitiesSection.test.tsx`:
  - header remains visible in every state; loading skeleton; success grid; empty message; error message with retry; retry returns to loading; announcements do not move focus; no duplicate content.
- `features/activities/components/ActivityGrid.test.tsx`:
  - 2 featured + 3 compact; 1 featured + compact; featured only (1 and 2) spans available width; upcoming-only feature-style grid up to 5 and max 3 columns; empty never renders a grid.
- `features/activities/components/ActivityCard.test.tsx`:
  - whole-card link, no nested link; title line clamps; optional categories/location omitted; image fallback; status badge text and non-color indicator; multi-day date rendering.
- `features/landing/components/HeroActions.test.tsx`:
  - guest Get Started targets login; authenticated Get Started targets the role dashboard; loading uses the guest-safe path; Explore uses the configured target.
- `features/landing/components/ServicesSection.test.tsx`:
  - guest vs authenticated vs loading; locked cards have no href and are inert/hidden; public cards usable; no overlay invitation; no layout-shift structure.
- `features/landing/components/SiteHeader.test.tsx`:
  - guest/auth/loading actions; dashboard path per role; mobile dialog focus restore and Escape; active link `aria-current`; login return path.
- `features/landing/components/GuideCard.test.tsx`:
  - whole-card link; unavailable destination is non-interactive and not a dead link.
- `components/ui/Button.test.tsx` (focused):
  - link vs button rendering; disabled/loading; variants do not bypass tokens.

Tests should target client components and pure functions. Next.js async Server Components are not rendered directly in Vitest; the route shell and metadata are verified through `npm run build` and the quickstart checks.

### Accessibility checks

- Run `axe-core` against key client renders (header, activities success/empty/error, services guest/auth) through a shared `expectNoA11yViolations` helper.
- Manual keyboard and screen-reader checks remain mandatory for the modal drawer, scroll-spy announcements, activity outcome announcements, and service gating.
- Automated checks supplement, but do not replace, the spec's manual verification.

### Manual and E2E coverage

- Use `quickstart.md` for the release verification matrix.
- Playwright is not added now. If the project later needs CI-level browser coverage, add it as a separate justified change; the current plan keeps runtime and test dependencies minimal.

## Risks and Assumptions

1. **Activity contract is unconfirmed.** The `{ data: ... }` envelope and field names are provisional. The service boundary, mapper, mock, and DTO isolate the change.
2. **Activity image host is unknown.** Mock mode uses local assets. Real mode requires a confirmed host in `images.remotePatterns`; do not guess a broad allowlist.
3. **Two service names/icons, hero headline, help destinations, and footer copy are pending.** The layout remains usable, and unavailable guide destinations must be presented as unavailable rather than dead links.
4. **The existing auth mock auto-authenticates every visitor, and its context memoization is stale.** `AuthProvider` hardcodes `mockAuthService`, its `getMe()` always returns a student, and its `useMemo` omits `isLoading`/`refreshUser`, so consumers may not observe auth-loading changes. The plan includes a minimal memoization fix (required for the header skeleton and services gating) and an optional mock-only `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_AUTH_STATE=guest|student|organizer|admin` scenario (default `student` to preserve current behavior); `AuthProvider` already clears the user when `getMe()` rejects. If maintainers reject the mock-only scenario, guest rendering is covered by component tests and manual QA waits for the real backend.
5. **The existing proxy has an unrelated authenticated-`/login` redirect issue** (the redirect is returned inside `forEach`). The landing flow does not depend on it for guests; do not expand this feature into a proxy refactor.
6. **No test runner exists.** Test tooling is a planned dev-only addition and must be reviewed under the dependency rule.
7. **Root route move is required.** Keeping both `src/app/page.tsx` and `src/app/(public)/page.tsx` would create a route conflict, so the old page is removed after migration.
8. **`next/image` API differences in Next 16.** Use `preload`, not `priority`, for the hero; verify the correct `sizes` and fallback behavior in the installed Next.js docs.

## Post-Design Constitution Re-check

Phase 1 artifacts (`research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/`, `quickstart.md`) are generated. Re-check result:

- No new runtime dependencies are introduced.
- No hardcoded colors are introduced in new components; all visual values map to the token layer.
- Routes and sibling features access only the public barrels `features/landing/index.ts` and `features/activities/index.ts`; shared layout receives navigation/footer data through props and shared `src/types`.
- The activity service contract, real/mock parity, DTO/domain split, and mapper boundary remain intact.
- All four activity states, auth-loading service gating, and header auth reservation remain explicit.
- Accessibility requirements are covered by semantics, native dialog behavior, focus restoration, reduced-motion handling, and automated plus manual checks.
- No constitutional violations or exceptions are required. The Complexity Tracking table remains empty.

277: 3. `start_time` or `end_time` is missing, not a string, not a valid date, or lacks an explicit timezone offset (`Z` or `┬▒HH:MM`).
278: 4. `end_time` is earlier than `start_time`.
279: 5. `registration_status` is not one of `open`, `upcoming`, or `closed`.
280: 
281: Normalization for usable records:
282: 
283: - Preserve the original `title` string.
284: - `image_url` blank/missing ΓåÆ `null`.
285: - `categories` missing/not an array ΓåÆ `[]`; remove blank strings.
286: - `location` blank/missing ΓåÆ `null`.
287: - `href` = `/activities/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`.
288: - Convert ISO strings to `Date` objects.
289: 
290: ### `mapLandingActivitiesDTO(dto: LandingActivitiesDTO): LandingActivities`
291: 
292: 1. Detect the shape:
293:    - Has `activities` array ΓåÆ single-list mode.
294:    - Has `featured` and/or `upcoming` arrays ΓåÆ grouped mode.
295:    - Both shapes present ΓåÆ throw `InvalidLandingActivitiesError` (`INVALID_PAYLOAD`).
296:    - Neither shape present ΓåÆ throw `InvalidLandingActivitiesError` (`INVALID_PAYLOAD`).
297: 2. Map each raw item with `mapActivityDTO`; collect valid items and count raw items.
298: 3. If raw item count > 0 and valid item count === 0 ΓåÆ throw `InvalidLandingActivitiesError`.
299: 4. Grouped mode:
300:    - A missing group is treated as an empty array.
301:    - `featured = validFeatured.slice(0, 2)`.
302:    - `upcoming = validUpcoming.slice(0, 3)`.
303:    - A group with invalid items but valid items in the other group does not throw.
304: 5. Single-list mode:
305:    - `featured = []`.
306:    - `upcoming = validItems.slice(0, 5)`.
307: 6. Return the domain collection.
308: 
309: ### Error type
310: 
311: ```ts
312: class InvalidLandingActivitiesError extends Error {
313:   readonly code: "INVALID_PAYLOAD" | "NO_USABLE_ITEMS";
314: }
315: ```
316: 
317: - `INVALID_PAYLOAD`: the response cannot be interpreted as either supported shape.
318: - `NO_USABLE_ITEMS`: raw items existed but none were usable.
319: - The hook converts either code into the error outcome. The UI uses fixed copy and never displays the raw error.
320: 
321: ## Activity State Machine
322: 
323: ```text
324: idle
325:   ΓööΓöÇ mount/refetch ΓåÆ loading
326:        Γö£ΓöÇ success (non-empty) ΓåÆ success
327:        Γö£ΓöÇ success (empty) ΓåÆ empty
328:        ΓööΓöÇ service/mapping failure ΓåÆ error
329: error
330:   ΓööΓöÇ refetch ΓåÆ loading
331: success/empty
332:   ΓööΓöÇ refetch ΓåÆ loading
333: ```
334: 
335: | State | `data` | `error` | UI body | Announcement |
336: |-------|--------|---------|---------|--------------|
337: | `loading` | `null` | `null` | Skeleton with 2 featured + 3 compact footprints | Busy status; polite announcement |
338: | `success` | `LandingActivities` | `null` | `ActivityGrid` | Loaded status; no focus move |
339: | `empty` | zero-item collection or `null` | `null` | EmptyState with reserved height | Empty status; no focus move |
340: | `error` | `null` | `Error` | ErrorState with Try again | Error status; no focus move |
341: 
342: **Transitions**:
343: - `refetch()` aborts the current request and enters `loading`.
344: - On retry, focus moves to the stable activity section heading/container rather than being dropped to the page start; the terminal outcome is announced without further focus movement.
345: - An aborted request never produces a visible state change.
346: - A response from an older request id is ignored.
347: - Repeated retries settle in exactly one terminal state.
348: - Unmount aborts the in-flight request.
349: 
350: ## Header and Navigation State
351: 
352: | State | Values | Behavior |
353: |-------|--------|----------|
354: | Auth action | `loading`, `guest`, `authenticated` | Reserved width; guest Log In; authenticated Dashboard |
355: | Mobile menu | `closed`, `open` | Native modal dialog; focus trap; scroll lock; Escape/backdrop close; focus restore |
356: | Active section | one of the tracked section ids | `aria-current="location"` plus underline/weight cue |
357: | Hash | empty or `#section` | Direct load, back/forward, and link activation restore the section |
358: 
359: **Invariants**:
360: - The header never shows Dashboard during auth loading.
361: - The mobile menu contains the same links and auth action as desktop.
362: - The rest of the page is inert while the modal menu is open.
363: - Closing without navigation returns focus to the menu trigger.
364: - Selecting a section closes the menu and moves focus to the section target.
365: 
366: ## Services State
367: 
368: | Auth state | Public services | Authenticated-only services |
369: |------------|-----------------|-----------------------------|
370: | `loading` | Usable | Locked, inert, hidden from assistive technology |
371: | `guest` | Usable | Locked, inert, hidden from assistive technology |
372: | `authenticated` | Usable | Usable, fully visible, real links |
373: 
374: **Invariants**:
375: - Locked cards are not links and have no destination in the DOM.
376: - Locked card text is not selectable.
377: - The same outer dimensions are used in all states to avoid layout shift.
378: - No separate sign-in invitation is rendered over locked cards.
379: - The header Log In action is the guest sign-in path.
380: 
381: ## Persistence and Boundaries
382: 
383: - No new persistence layer.
384: - Activity data is fetched at runtime; no caching or global store is introduced in this feature.
385: - The existing session cookie remains owned by the auth layer; the landing page never reads it directly.
386: - Config modules are static at build time; pending content is updated in one place.
387: - DTOs never cross the service/mapper boundary into components.

1: # Contract: Activity Service and Hook
2: 
3: **Feature**: `001-landing-page` | **Status**: Planned
4: 
5: The activity feature exposes one data operation through a TypeScript service contract. The real and mock implementations are interchangeable at a single selection point. Components and hooks consume domain models only.
6: 
7: ## Service Interface
8: 
9: ```ts
10: // features/activities/services/activity.service.ts
11: export interface ActivityService {
12:   getLandingActivities(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<LandingActivities>;
13: }
14: ```
15: 
16: ### Method contract
17: 
18: `getLandingActivities(signal?)`:
19: 
20: - Resolves with a display-ready `LandingActivities` domain collection.
21: - Rejects when the request fails, the response is malformed, or raw items were supplied but none are usable.
22: - Honors `signal` by aborting the underlying request.
23: - Does not expose DTOs, the response envelope, or HTTP status details to callers.
24: 
25: ## Implementations
26: 
27: ### RealActivityService
28: 
29: - Calls `api.get<LandingActivitiesResponseDTO>("/activities/landing", { signal })`.
30: - Passes `response.data` to `mapLandingActivitiesDTO`.
31: - Returns the mapped domain collection.
32: - Does not call `fetch` directly.
33: - Does not construct a base URL.
34: - Does not handle auth headers; the public endpoint requires none.
35: 
36: ### MockActivityService
37: 
38: - Implements the same interface and returns domain values through the same mapper used by the real service.
39: - Uses deterministic DTO fixtures.
40: - Simulates a short latency and supports cancellation.
41: - Supports these scenarios:
42:   - `success`: grouped data with 2 featured and 3 upcoming.
43:   - `partial`: grouped data containing some invalid items alongside usable items.
44:   - `empty`: a valid 200 response with no activities.
45:   - `error`: a rejected request with a normalized error.
46:   - `delay`: a slow request for loading-state verification.
47:   - `single-list`: a valid single ordered list with 3ΓÇô5 items.
48:   - `all-invalid`: raw items supplied but none usable, producing the error outcome.
49:   - `long-content`: long titles, missing optional fields, a multi-day activity, and an image failure for edge-case QA.
50: 
51: - Scenario selection for manual QA uses `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_ACTIVITY_SCENARIO`; tests inject the mock or a deferred fake directly.
52: 
53: ## Selection Point
54: 
55: ```ts
56: // features/activities/services/activity.service.factory.ts
57: export function createActivityService(): ActivityService;
58: ```
59: 
60: - This is the only production module that imports both implementations.
61: - `src/libs/service-mode.ts` reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE`.
62: - `mock` is the default until the backend contract is confirmed.
63: - `api` selects the real implementation.
64: - No component or hook imports `MockActivityService` directly.
65: 
66: ## Hook Contract
67: 
68: ```ts
69: // features/activities/hooks/useLandingActivities.ts
70: export type LandingActivitiesStatus =
71:   | "loading"
72:   | "success"
73:   | "empty"
74:   | "error";
75: 
76: export type UseLandingActivitiesResult =
77:   | {
78:       status: "loading";
79:       data: null;
80:       error: null;
81:       refetch: () => void;
82:     }
83:   | {
84:       status: "success";
85:       data: LandingActivities;
86:       error: null;
87:       refetch: () => void;
88:     }
89:   | {
90:       status: "empty";
91:       data: LandingActivities;
92:       error: null;
93:       refetch: () => void;
94:     }
95:   | {
96:       status: "error";
97:       data: null;
98:       error: Error;
99:       refetch: () => void;
100:     };
101: 
102: export function useLandingActivities(): UseLandingActivitiesResult;
103: ```
104: 
105: ### Hook behavior
106: 
107: - Starts in `loading` on mount.
108: - Calls `createActivityService().getLandingActivities(signal)`.
109: - Treats a successful collection with no items as `empty`.
110: - Treats service and mapping failures as `error`.
111: - `refetch()` aborts the previous request and returns to `loading`.
112: - Aborts on unmount.
113: - Ignores aborted requests and responses from older request ids.
114: - Never throws during render; errors are represented in the state.
115: - Does not log raw sensitive payloads.
116: 
117: ### Test injection
118: 
119: For tests, the hook may accept an optional service argument:
120: 
121: ```ts
122: export function useLandingActivities(
123:   service?: ActivityService,
124: ): UseLandingActivitiesResult;
125: ```
126: 
127: The default remains `createActivityService()`. Production call sites pass nothing. Tests pass a fake/deferred service to control timing and outcomes without environment variables.
128: 
129: ## Domain Types
130: 
131: The service returns:
132: 
133: ```ts
134: type LandingActivities = {
135:   featured: Activity[];
136:   upcoming: Activity[];
137: };
138: ```
139: 
140: - `featured` is explicit-group featured content only; it is empty for single-list responses.
141: - `upcoming` is either explicit-group upcoming content or single-list content.
142: - Invalid items are removed.
143: - Display caps are applied after filtering: grouped ΓåÆ 2 featured / 3 upcoming; single list ΓåÆ 5 upcoming.
144: - No DTO fields (`image_url`, `start_time`, `registration_status`) reach the hook or UI.
145: 
146: ## Error Semantics
147: 
148: | Failure | Service result | Hook state |
149: |---------|----------------|------------|
150: | Network error | rejects with normalized `Error` | error |
151: | 5xx | rejects with normalized `Error` | error |
152: | Malformed payload | rejects with `InvalidLandingActivitiesError` (`INVALID_PAYLOAD`) | error |
153: | Raw items but all invalid | rejects with `InvalidLandingActivitiesError` (`NO_USABLE_ITEMS`) | error |
154: | Valid 200 with no items | resolves with empty collection | empty |
155: | Aborted request | rejects with an abort error; caller ignores it | no visible change |
156: 
157: The UI never displays the raw error message. It displays the fixed activity error copy and a Try again action.
158: 
159: ## Behavioral Compatibility Checklist
160: 
161: The mock and real implementations must both satisfy:
162: 
163: - Same method signature and return type.
164: - Same empty/success/error semantics.
165: - Same cancellation behavior.
166: - Same mapper boundary and domain shape.
167: - No DTO leakage.
168: - No environment-specific branching inside consumers.
169: - No production import of the mock except through the factory.

(End of file - total 169 lines)
</content>

2: 
3: **Feature**: `001-landing-page` | **Status**: Planned
4: 
5: These contracts keep the landing page on the shared component layers required by the constitution. Generic primitives live in `src/components/ui`; site chrome lives in `src/components/layout`; landing- and activity-specific composition stays in features.
6: 
7: ## Generic Primitives (`src/components/ui`)
8: 
9: ### Button
10: 
11: ```ts
12: type ButtonProps = {
13:   variant: "primary" | "secondary" | "white" | "ghost";
14:   size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg";
15:   href?: string;
16:   isLoading?: boolean;
17:   leftIcon?: React.ReactNode;

21:   onClick?: React.MouseEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>;

23:   className?: string;
24: };
25: ```
26: 
27: Behavior:
28: 
29: - Renders `next/link` when `href` is present; otherwise renders `<button>`.
30: - Loading state keeps an accessible name and sets `aria-busy="true"`; it does not render a spinner-only control.

1: # Quickstart: Public Landing Page
2: 
3: **Feature**: `001-landing-page` | **Date**: 2026-11-13
4: 
5: This guide is for implementation and verification of the landing page. It assumes the feature plan has been implemented. It does not replace the specification or the contracts.
6: 
7: ## Prerequisites
8: 
9: - Node.js compatible with the project's Next.js 16 setup.
10: - Dependencies installed from the repository root of the client app.
11: - Read `AGENTS.md` before changing Next.js code. This project uses Next.js 16 conventions (`proxy.ts`, `preload` instead of `priority`).
12: - Do not commit secrets or a real backend URL in `.env.local`.
13: 
14: ## Install and Run
15: 
16: From `src/client`:
17: 
18: ```powershell
19: npm install
20: npm run dev
21: ```
22: 
23: Open `http://localhost:3000`.
24: 
25: Quality gates:
26: 
27: ```powershell
28: npm run lint
29: npm run build
30: npm test
31: ```
32: 
33: `npm test` is available after the test-tooling task adds Vitest and the test scripts. Until then, use `npm run lint` and `npm run build`, and run the manual checks below.
34: 
35: ## Mock Configuration
36: 
37: Create an untracked `.env.local` for local verification:
38: 
39: ```dotenv
40: NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE=mock
41: NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_ACTIVITY_SCENARIO=success
42: NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_AUTH_STATE=student
43: ```
44: 
45: | Variable | Values | Purpose |
46: |----------|--------|---------|
47: | `NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE` | `mock` (default), `api` | Selects the activity service implementation |
48: | `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_ACTIVITY_SCENARIO` | `success`, `partial`, `empty`, `error`, `delay`, `single-list`, `all-invalid`, `long-content` | Selects deterministic activity fixtures |
49: | `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_AUTH_STATE` | `guest`, `student`, `organizer`, `admin` | Optional mock-auth QA scenario; default preserves the existing signed-in mock behavior |
50: 
51: `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are embedded at build time. Restart the dev server after changing them.
52: 
53: ### Real service configuration
54: 
55: When the backend contract is confirmed:
56: 
57: ```dotenv
58: NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE=api
59: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=https://your-confirmed-api.example
60: ```
61: 
62: Do not enable this until the endpoint, response envelope, field names, and image host are confirmed. If activity images are remote, add the confirmed host to `images.remotePatterns`; do not use a broad allowlist.
63: 
64: ## Verification Matrix
65: 
66: ### 1. Static page and composition
67: 
68: 1. Open `/` with activities in `delay` mode.
69: 2. Confirm the header, hero, highlights, help, and footer render before the activity request completes.
70: 3. Confirm there is exactly one `h1`, section titles are `h2`, and card titles are `h3`.
71: 4. Confirm the six sections appear in order: Hero, Highlights, Activities, Services, Help, Footer.
72: 5. Confirm the page metadata title, description, and social preview are present.
73: 6. Confirm the footer copyright year matches the current year and is not a hardcoded value.
74: 
75: ### 2. Guest behavior
76: 
77: 1. Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_AUTH_STATE=guest`.
78: 2. Confirm the header shows Log In and reserves its space without a Dashboard flash.
79: 3. Confirm Get Started opens `/login` and, after successful sign-in, lands on the role dashboard.
80: 4. Confirm header Log In from the services area returns to `/#services` after sign-in.
81: 5. Confirm public services are usable and authenticated-only services are blurred, inert, unselectable, and absent from the accessibility tree.
82: 6. Confirm there is no ΓÇ£Log in to see all servicesΓÇ¥ overlay.
83: 
84: ### 3. Signed-in behavior
85: 
86: 1. Set the mock auth state to `student`, then repeat for `organizer` and `admin`.
87: 2. Confirm `/` does not redirect away.
88: 3. Confirm the header shows Dashboard and links to the correct role dashboard.
89: 4. Confirm all services are visible and usable.
90: 5. Confirm Get Started goes directly to the role dashboard.
91: 
92: ### 4. Activity states
93: 
94: Use the mock scenario variable and reload `/` for each case:
95: 
96: | Scenario | Expected |
97: |----------|----------|
98: | `success` | Two featured cards on the left and three compact cards on the right on wide screens |
99: | `partial` | Invalid records are omitted; valid records still render |
100: | `empty` | Empty message with reserved height; no empty grid |
101: | `error` | Error message and Try again; the rest of the page remains usable |
102: | `delay` | Skeleton persists; header and other sections remain usable |
103: | `single-list` | Up to five featured-style cards, at most three columns |
104: | `all-invalid` | Error outcome; no broken cards |
105: | `long-content` | Four-line featured title clamp, three-line compact clamp, multi-day date, missing optional fields omitted, image fallback |
106: 
107: Retry:
108: 
109: 1. Start in `error`.
110: 2. Activate Try again repeatedly.
111: 3. Confirm the section enters loading and ends in exactly one success, empty, or error outcome with no duplicate content.
112: 
113: ### 5. Navigation
114: 
115: 1. Click each header link; confirm the section lands below the floating header and the URL hash updates.
116: 2. Scroll through the page; confirm the active link updates and uses more than color.
117: 3. Open `/#services` directly; confirm the services section is positioned correctly after images/fonts finish loading.
118: 4. Use browser Back and Forward; confirm the previous/next section is restored.
119: 5. Open the brand; confirm it returns to the top.
120: 
121: ### 6. Mobile drawer
122: 
123: Use a viewport below 1024px:
124: 
125: 1. Open the menu; confirm it is modal, contains all section links and the auth action, and locks page scrolling.
126: 2. Press Tab repeatedly; confirm focus stays inside the drawer.
127: 3. Press Escape; confirm the drawer closes and focus returns to the menu trigger.
128: 4. Activate the backdrop; confirm the drawer closes and focus returns to the trigger.
129: 5. Select a section; confirm the drawer closes and the page moves to that section.
130: 
131: ### 7. Responsive layout
132: 
133: Check at 320, 375, 640, 768, 1024, 1440, and 1920 pixels wide.
134: 
135: - 320ΓÇô639: one column for highlights, services, and guides; hero actions stack; compact activities stay horizontal.
136: - 640ΓÇô1023: header uses the menu; highlights and services use two columns; guides use two columns; featured activities use two columns; compact activities form a two-column stack below.
137: - 1024+: three highlight columns; 3x2 services; 2x2 guides; featured/compact activity arrangement as designed.
138: - No horizontal scrolling at any width.
139: - Touch targets are at least 44x44px.
140: 
141: ### 8. Accessibility
142: 
143: 1. Navigate the entire page by keyboard; every interactive element is reachable in a logical order with visible focus.
144: 2. Confirm the activity section announces loading/empty/error without moving focus.
145: 3. Confirm status labels include text and are not color-only.
146: 4. Confirm decorative images/shapes are hidden and content images have meaningful alternatives.
147: 5. Confirm the mobile drawer excludes the rest of the page from keyboard and screen-reader navigation.
148: 6. Enable reduced motion; confirm scrolling is immediate, hover lift is suppressed, and skeleton pulse is disabled.
149: 7. Run `axe-core` checks (once the test helper exists) and review the report for critical violations.
150: 8. Check text contrast at WCAG 2.1 AA, especially the hero headline over the campus image and white text on the deep-blue services/footer backgrounds.
151: 
152: ### 9. Images and resilience
153: 
154: 1. Force the hero image to fail; confirm the layout remains intact and the text stays readable.
155: 2. Force an activity image to fail; confirm the branded placeholder preserves card dimensions.
156: 3. Use an invalid image URL in a mock fixture; confirm no layout shift.
157: 4. Throttle the network; confirm the activity skeleton does not block the rest of the page.
158: 
159: ### 10. Activity contract edge cases
160: 
161: 1. A single ordered list is treated as upcoming and rendered in the featured style.
162: 2. A single list after grouped placeholders may reflow without clipping, overlap, or horizontal scrolling.
163: 3. An activity with no categories or location omits those lines without punctuation artifacts.
164: 4. A multi-day activity displays both dates and times in `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`.
165: 5. A title with Vietnamese text renders exactly as supplied, with no case transformation.
166: 6. Extra featured/upcoming items are ignored beyond the display caps.
167: 
168: ## Automated Test Targets
169:
